title: Review finite live AWS proof invocation and private credential-delivery adapter
description: Bounded follow-up after offline helper source/fault-test acceptance, before ANY actual credential read or AWS use. The current awspermission library deliberately has no executable CLI/profile loader/approvalfile parser. Review exact invocation/config+tree+binary approval, explicit short-lived SSO-derived credential parent/pipe delivery (no output/cache/ambient fallback or refresh), independently pinned private os.Root journal and per-phase exact account/resource/expiry/call budget. Strict bounded private files/no symlink/FIFO/unknownfields; durable one-shot markers/no automatic replay after unknown; safe result/error/private log capture. Root owns each later concrete authorization. This issue does not authorize authenticated preflight, plan/apply, seeds, AssumeRole/probes or cleanup. Preserve candidate/canary deny-all and production untouched.
design:
A. Boundary and exact files (proposal ONLY; no source/auth reads yet)
Keep accepted helper core/config/credentials/journal/sdk/run files unchanged. Add awspermission/invocation.go (finite wire types/preflight/ExecuteInvocation/offline initializer), invocation_files.go (bounded private canonical JSON/files/outside-pin), invocation_test.go (synthetic local-I/O/fault tests), cmd/run-aws-readproof/main.go and cmd/init-aws-readproof-journal/main.go. Update existing awspermission/README.md only. No module/provider/common/fixture artifact edits. This task is design review; implementation gets a separate bounded child after root accepts.

B. Small canonical wire, no generic configuration framework
InvocationV1 fixed ordered fields: Version=1, Contract=registry-aws-readproof-invocation-v1, Account=429214323166, Region=us-west-2, ProofID=fixture-20261030-01-aws-readproof, SourceFreezeSHA256, BinarySHA256, JournalPinSHA256, Config. Config is a finite DTO copying existing Config EXCEPT Now: Phase, Bindings(the existing exact ReadProofBindings), SourceAdminRoleID, FixtureExpiresAt, DenyFixtureExpiresAt, ApprovedUntil, ApprovalSHA256. Config digest stays EXACT existing ConfigurationDigest; no new digest substituting for it. Whole invocation raw SHA comes independently in parent argv, not in itself. Source/Binary SHA are externally reviewed audit refs, NOT code attestation or permission. PinV1 fixed fields: Version=1, Contract=registry-aws-readproof-journal-pin-v1, Binding(existing JournalBinding incl independently pinned BootstrapUID/SpecSHA256/ManifestSHA256/Directory FileID). Raw pin SHA separately in parent argv and must equal Invocation.JournalPinSHA256. Finite wire uses exact json.Marshal(struct)+one newline bytes, UTC-Z timestamps; strict decoder+EOF+byte-identical re-encode rejects duplicate, case-alias, unknown nested fields, whitespace variants and trailing content. Invocation <=32KiB, pin<=8KiB. Do not add arbitrary endpoint/action/profile/path selectors inside JSON.

C. Public API and fixed commands
ExecuteInvocation(ctx context.Context, o InvocationOptions, credentialPipe *os.File) (Result,error). Options exactly InvocationPath, ExpectedInvocationSHA256, JournalDirectory, JournalPinPath, ExpectedJournalPinSHA256. Public implementation owns time.Now and fixed New+Run; no public clock/factory/permit callback. Private typed clock/executor/reader seams for synchronous synthetic tests only. CLI run-aws-readproof has exactly the five safe metadata flags above, no positional arguments/phase/action/profile/credential flag; phase only from pinned Invocation. Uses inherited FD3 anonymous pipe ONLY, stdin unused, never filesystem FIFO fallback. No spawn, aws/config, profile loader, environment credential access, refresh, endpoint override, key file or bootstrap fallback. Output uses existing bounded safe Result plus closed finite diagnostic, never raw err.Error/panic/provider payload. No automatic loop/retry/recovery mode.

D. Pre-credential order and limits
1) Parse exact flags; validate canonical absolute metadata/root paths and safe SHA syntax; refuse canceled context. 2) Open only explicit invocation/pin metadata: every existing path component no symlink; immediate parent owned0700; file regular0600/currentUID/Nlink1, bounded size, nofollow+nonblock, lstat/open inode equality, exact independent raw digests; canonical finite decode. 3) Require fixed account/region/proof/source+binary hash syntax, exact pin hash equality, existing config digest and phase, real-clock freshness/<=15m, deadline <= BOTH parent fixture expiries, native binding structure/phase seed-vs-probe gate. No credentials read to discover invalidity. 4) Open exact existing owned0700 os.Root and OpenJournal with externally pinned Binding; exact directory+manifest/spec/UID equality, no creation/adoption. Pin must be outside journal. Require only identity.json present for a fresh invocation; ANY requested/receipt/unknown file denies before credentials. 5) Require FD3 *os.File ModeNamedPipe/currentUID anonymous-pipe handle, supports SetReadDeadline BEFORE any Read, deadline=min(realNow+10s, approval, ctxdeadline). Parent sets inherited read end nonblocking before pass; reject unsupported deadlines, no goroutine fallback. Close owned pipe on every return; EOF required by bounded DecodeBootstrapCredentials. 6) Decode only synthetic/live separately approved supplied stream; reject credential expiry before overall min(approval,now+5m) budget, clip usable deadline through existing New. Recheck config/ctx/journal before New+Run. Existing helper writes/fsyncs SourceIdentity Requested before first SDK dispatch and all later steps. No extra durable pre-read tombstone proposed: reading credentials is not AWS mutation; existing provider-dispatch one-shot barrier plus fresh-journal check suffices for managed single-parent invocation. Concurrent losing processes might read their explicit stream but cannot dispatch second SourceIdentity because O_EXCL; no at-most-one credential-read/distributed claim. Parent launches exactly once and never auto-replays.

E. Offline journal initialization without a circular approval
InitializeInvocationJournal(ctx, InitOptions) returns finite InitReceipt{Contract,Outcome,PinSHA256}. InitOptions exactly existing-new JournalDirectory, absent external PinPath, BootstrapUID64hex, ConfigurationSHA25664hex. Root can calculate/review Config digest before pin exists; init needs no Invocation/credentials/cloud. Require precreated EMPTY owned0700 journal root; private owned0700 pin parent OUTSIDE journal; no symlink/FIFO/path fallback. Existing BootstrapJournal creates identity O_EXCL/fsync/readback; write canonical PinV1 outside root O_EXCL0600/fsync/readback+parent fsync. Never create missing directory on reopen, overwrite existing pin, reset/prune/import/adopt a partial init. Unknown file/fsync results retain all files and return finite Unproven/no fabricated init ACK. Parent separately retains/inspects pin then writes exact Invocation binding its SHA, binary/source refs and existing Config. A new approved root cannot be used to bypass earlier unknown outcome; that remains an external parent invariant with retained independent pins, not cryptographic rollback resistance. Init CLI only four safe metadata flags, stdin unused and no FD3 read.

F. Binary/source/authority review remains independent
Before any live invocation, root independently verifies frozen source hash, exact readonly offline build/module graph, private owned immutable binary directory/file/hash, current account+SSO role/birth/resource/policy/headroom, exact config bytes/digest, and exact outside-pin/root identity; then authorizes a single command. Runtime binary/source fields are audit equality refs ONLY. Hashing os.Executable by pathname is not a reliable proof of currently mapped code after pathname replacement, so do not present a self-hash as authentication. Controlled local no-concurrent-writer/clean-handoff assumptions remain explicit. Expected invocation/pin digests in argv are safe equality pins, not signed approval. Actual SSO-profile AWSCLI export/privatepipe parent command and its authentication/refresh behavior need separate concrete review before credential reads. This adapter never starts it.

G. Meaningful pure/local synthetic tests, no network/exec
Independent spy reader verifies zero credential bytes for invalid phase/account/region/proof/hash, source/binary malformed refs, nested duplicate/case-alias/unknown/trailing JSON, expired/overlong/parent-expiring config, wrong pin/spec/UID/root inode/manifest, missing or replaced root/pin, symlink/FIFO/hardlink/oversize/permission metadata, prior step/unknown journal entry, canceled context. Owned os.Pipe cases verify only explicit handle, EOF/one bounded JSON, nonpipe refusal, working finite deadline/cancel/stalled producer, no unsupported-deadline goroutine. Private synthetic executor tests exact config/clock/pins passed, single execution, safe finite results/errors/panic handling and credentials closed; no real SDK factory is invoked by these adapter tests. Existing helper tests independently cover actual generated SDK fakeHTTP+6/11 orchestration. Init tests empty/outside exclusive success, missing/nonempty/unsafe root, inside/existing pin refusal, partial/unknown write retained and no replay/reset. Sentinel credential strings absent from JSON/fmt/diagnostic/error on every tested result, including provider/panic/private filesystem errors. No child process, host FD inheritance, TLS wire or live AWS permission claim; actual FD3 process handoff needs a separately reviewed owned tier or reviewed live-parent gate later.

H. Failure/closure semantics
Report only closed finite diagnostic codes and exact validated Result prefix/step count/hash/enum/request-ID fields, not native SDK objects, arbitrary exception text or private paths. Same-goroutine panic becomes finite Unproven, drops raw panic and retains any existing markers; no continuing execution. No reconstruction of terminal ACK after unknown; stdout emission failure is nonzero exit and never authorizes replay. Approval/context expiry at any point stops; material and transports close through existing accepted Helper. Budget remains Seed6/Probe11, max1 start/sec, RPC10s, overall5m, approval<=15m and both fixture TTLs. Candidate/canary/build remain denyall; no policy update, Terraform, admin credential generation, permission test, clean-up or Temporal operation is authorized by this design.

One fixed phase Seed6 or Probe11, no genericservice/action/target selector, no autojournalbootstrap/reopen/adoption/reset/retry. title: Design an owned authorized source outage browser proof without deleting evidence
description: Read-only bounded design for remaining actual authorized source-unavailable browser criterion. Existing exact10 proof/public assets stay frozen. Compare canonical owned journal ConfigMap UID/RV deletion versus closing a separately bound exact read-only local TLS journal proxy after real successful reader/browser load. Preserve original evidence, use actual PinnedDesired/live policy/Session/JournalSource/Model/handler, no fake source/API or browser admin route. Propose finite paths/phases/counters/security/cleanup; no source/tests/cluster/cloud calls.
design:
Recommend a SEPARATE owned-local source-connector outage case, not mutation/deletion of the journal and not an extension/rerun of the accepted exact10 browser proof. The existing public UI assets and current10 behavioral cases remain unchanged. Prefer closing a real exact read-only local TLS proxy used ONLY by the new reader Repository. It forwards real owned API GETs before closure; it never synthesizes diagnostic JSON, source snapshots or Kubernetes error statuses. Closing/draining its listener/connections creates an actual transport failure. Claim source-connector unavailability, not Kubernetes-wide outage: underlying API/policy/desired remain healthy and are independently observed directly.

Tradeoff: exact UID/RV conditional deletion of the owned journal is fewer fixture lines and would produce a real backend404 mapped to HTTP503 for a previously registered pinned source. It irreversibly destroys the canonical source/evidence and prevents recovery without a new UID/adoption, obscuring the evidence-retention principle. The read-only proxy adds a private listener/trust setup but preserves evidence, exercises the real JournalSource/Repository/Model/Handler error path and needs no production hook/new service. Do not introduce a general source interface, HTTP fault toggle or generic proxy target.

Proposed finite implementation paths for later root review: NEW operator-v2/integration/zzzzz_local_page_source_unavailable_test.go (integration&&browser_integration; exact TestLocalDiagnosticSourceUnavailableAfterWriterExit), NEW integration/runtime_browser_source_unavailable_test.go (exact TLS read-proxy/helper), NEW scripts/operator_browser_source_unavailable.mjs (separate finite page sequence), and NEW scripts/tests/browser_source_unavailable_protocol.test.mjs if its private protocol parser is factored for import. Existing scripts/operator_browser_kube_fixture.py and run_operator_kube_tests.py would get one separately reviewed finite --diagnostic-browser-source-unavailable selection, mutually exclusive with existing browser/--tests modes, exact mandatory boundary+new one test; no arbitrary mode/URL/command/source parameter. Existing runtime_browser_wire_test.go needs at most a test-only constructor extraction/overload accepting an independently constructed pinned Repository for this new case; existing newBrowserPageFixture wrapper/old ten assertions preserve their direct source behavior. Avoid duplicating auth/policy/UI construction or exporting a production injection hook. If absolute byte freeze forbids that helper extraction, defer it explicitly rather than silently replacing a source or duplicating another auth stack. No edits are authorized by this design task.

Private setup: reuse actual owned Service403/404 writer fixture and synchronous wait/reap; final writer canonical receipt/cause retained before reader/listener creation. Independently read actual journal UID/RV/canonical bytes and retain private comparison digest. Create separate loopback tcp4 TLS server with the exact Go httptest fixture certificate pinned as explicit leaf trust and explicit owned mTLS client configuration (owned loopback; no per-run CA/key freshness claim) (no ambient CA/proxy/kubeconfig/credential lookup, no global TLS bypass); bind upstream fixed approved local.Server and existing owned local client transport. Its finite request allowlist is GET ONLY, no body/query/encoded aliases: /api/v1/namespaces/kube-system, /api/v1/namespaces/<exact trusted control Parent.Ref.Name>, /api/v1/namespaces/<that namespace>/configmaps/<exact trusted Cell.Record.Ref.Name>. Client.New/namespace binding refreshes use the first two paths; pinned Cell.Read uses the third. No PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE, no discovery/list/watch or policy/desired routing through this connector. Proxy logging/error output fixed/discarded, listener private to Go container, endpoint/CA never sent to browser.

Fresh reader composes actual kubejournal.Cell+Repository via that exact connector; real independently pinned Desired and live Policy stay on the direct owned API binding, with actual SessionAuthorizer/Model/Handler/NewLocalPage unchanged. Synthetic HMAC issuance is explicitly fixture-only; actual session verification/current policy checks remain real. Source wrapper only counts calls and cannot manufacture data. The new browser uses the same four frozen public UI assets and exact fixed same-origin paths; no admin browser route. Native/sandbox/startup proof must still apply to this new actual browser/container, not be borrowed from the earlier run. A new small fixed entry script may reuse existing assertion primitives and the reviewed host container controls; either include its own bounded startup checks or obtain a separate reviewed shared-startup extraction without changing existing10 assertions. Do not add arbitrary driver/CDP/env/TLS overrides. No new acquisition needed if exact existing pinned artifacts are present; missing cache fails closed.

Finite phases: start -> ready -> disconnect-source -> source-disconnected -> finish -> finished. Initial browser explicit Load requires binding200 for same canonical target and diagnostic200 from actual journal, old primary cause visible; sourceReads exactly1. Browser signals disconnect over owned parent private stdio, never HTTP. Go asserts completed first read/no in-flight source callback, then closes/drains exact TLS proxy (including idle keepalive connections), and marks it permanently closed; no resume/recreate phase. Repeat/unknown phases are rejected. Direct independently pinned API reads verify journal UID/RV/canonical payload unchanged and policy+desired exact pins/content intact after closure. Only finite booleans/counters leave Go, not bytes/UID/RV/paths/proxy URL/cookie/header/error detail.

Second explicit manual Load must still get binding200/same target, then actual HTTP503 with exact {error:DiagnosticSourceUnavailable}, NOT AuthorizationUnavailable503 or authorization/notfound404. Exactly one additional counted Source.Read, final total2; no automatic load/poll/recovery. The proxy may fail during the adapter cluster/parent refresh before the Cell GET; this is still real source-connector failure, not proof the Kubernetes server is down or a ConfigMap is missing. Browser verifies prior Original cause/protected content existed before click, then old cause headings/details absent and exact existing generic service-unavailable/previous-protected-view-cleared message after failure. Page already clears on explicit refresh: report that lifecycle outcome honestly, not a stronger claim that old DOM persists until HTTP failure. Inspect response status/constant code privately; no raw DOM/error/header/cookie snapshots in receipts.

Finish acceptance: final sourceReads exactly2, source route bound/registered throughout, direct journal/policy/desired unchanged and accessible, original managed Service POST counter stays1 (NO new managed/provider mutation after writer exit), source proxy closed, no writer reopened, no cleanup/delete/recreate used to manufacture outage. title: Design actor terminal auth-observation receipt integration
description: Root requests bounded read-only actor integration proposal after backend .9.6.8 focus acceptance. Define fresh registry/metadata/read-settings policy discrimination, expected endpoint digest from public pure helper rather than response learning/hash duplication, terminal Record API and historical result/current authority separation, timeout/duration/capacity/read closure semantics, finite expired failure handling and original-fault versus uncertain receipt outcomes. Existing stage/read lane/default schemas unchanged. No code/tests/cloud/tag calls; root review before implementation.
design:
READ-ONLY ACTOR TERMINAL AUTH-RECEIPT INTEGRATION PROPOSAL. No implementation/tests/cloud/tag execution in this task. Existing backend .8 remains subject to fresh Linux aggregate; actual actor recording needs its own child and owned TLS proof.

A. Explicit fresh lane/discrimination. Add Mode LocalDisposableStagingAuthReceipts (new string), requiring BOTH nonnil MetadataConfig.AuthObservationPolicy and nonzero RegistryConfig.AuthObservationPolicyDigest. Existing LocalDisposableStaging must require both zero; existing stage-only/read-only registry+checkpoint bytes/schemas unchanged. New registry digest field appended with omitempty at zero. New registry schema staging-auth-observation-receipts-v1 requires ObservationBindingDigest nonzero. Independently compute AuthObservationPolicyDigest from named domain temporal-candidate-auth-observation-policy-binding-v1 + normalized copied policy + exact MetadataBinding.ConfigSHA256 + existing ObservationBindingDigest; this is bootstrap provenance only. Public pure policy fingerprint helper may be exposed for coordinator bootstrap; it grants no authority. Constructor deep-copies metadata policy before retaining Config, then opens independently pinned new metadata root and matches its policy/config digest, existing read settings/KMS fingerprint, exact public endpoint binding, and fresh registry digest BEFORE admission claim. No first response/policy learning, migration or in-place enable/disable. All create/advance behavior remains staging-only/default manager capabilities and immutable failure policy unchanged.

B. Pure endpoint helper without v1 wire break. Current Observer endpoint digest is computed privately in observe.go from canonical struct fields Cloud,Data,Trust,Project,API; it is NOT the actor settings/KMS digest. Propose credentialobservation.ExpectedEndpointBinding(EndpointBindingInput{Cloud,Data,TrustBindingID,ProjectID}) -> EndpointBinding{Schema:1,Contract:temporal-candidate-namespace-auth-endpoints-v1,Digest},error. Inputs contain only public typed configuration, no dependency/secret/transport/factory/Now/observed response; API version fixed to tc.SupportedAPIVersion. Reuse existing identifier+endpointTLS validation and the SINGLE private v1 canonical hash implementation, extracted from observe.go; actual Observer output and pure helper must use that same implementation over copied config. Digest remains EXACT existing v1 bytes/domain-shaped canonical object, so stage/read DTO contract and old registry settings fingerprint do not change. The typed helper contract explicitly identifies its v1 hash domain; do not claim a new cryptographic prefix was added. A genuinely new prefixed/hash domain would require a separate future observation contract/version. Constructor computes expected endpoint digest locally BEFORE any network and compares it to fresh metadata policy.EndpointBindingDigest; never obtain expected value from first observed proof or duplicate opaque struct hashing in actor. New registry policy fingerprint has explicit domain tag independently.

C. Duration/clock. Existing read-only settings.Timeout bound unchanged. Fresh receipt lane additionally requires Timeout+1second persistence reserve <= policy.MaximumDuration <=10sec (finite reserve, not a promise filesystem I/O always completes in1sec). Record API has bounded caller-derived overall context up to MaximumDuration, nested accepted read budget up to Timeout; never context.Background/ignore caller cancellation. This leaves a bounded parent-alive interval to persist a finite nested read timeout. Closure/post-authority/append may still exceed remaining budget, yielding no receipt ACK. Success receipt.StartedAt comes from exact Observer result; failure start captures trusted clock immediately before read/known-expiry decision. RecordedAt is trusted clock captured immediately before Insert and passed as identical now; it is event recording time, NOT durable commit/ACK time. Store validation remains duration/expiry bounded; actual actor must not accept an arbitrarily stale successful proof.

D. Public API/result. Add RecordObservationRequest{ObserveRequest,AttemptID hex64}; AttemptID stable explicit caller-owned identity, not automatically incremented on retry. RecordAuthObservation returns RecordObservationResult{ReceiptAcknowledgement enum NotAttempted/Recorded/Historical/Unknown/Rejected, Receipt *typed terminal receipt optional, ObservationFailure *finite Code+Step optional},error. Errors are safe finite lifecycle/persistence errors only, never raw SDK/store/client text. New finite auth failure with successful record returns Recorded receipt+original finite failure (and may return same safe observation error); historical lookup returns Historical original receipt/time/session, never a new check/freshness result, even if now expired. On receipt uncertainty return Unknown with NO acknowledged Receipt and preserve known original finite auth failure separately; persistence error must not overwrite it. Pure capacity/validation denial before TLS is NotAttempted/Rejected with no false candidate failure. Exact historical failed receipt is historical retrieval, not new current auth failure. Final naming/error convention can be tightened in implementation review; it must keep these independent facts.

E. Exact lifecycle/order. Hold existing actor mu+registry lifecycle lock throughout. Reject closed/disabled/caller auth headers/cancellation exactly as accepted. Check current gate/session/writer/registry/policy; load structurally validated paired Staged+MetadataVerified state. Build exact AuthObservationRequest including canonical ARN/resource birth and independent Journal+Outcome versions. AuthObservations.Preflight FIRST compares existing stable request refs and bounded capacity; it never compares a NEW actor session to the historical stored session. A matching historical terminal record returns Historical after CURRENT authority is independently rechecked; no namespace/secret/TLS calls, no timestamp/session replacement. Missing record with capacity may proceed. There is NO Requested record and NO new receipt-state gate on ObserveStaged. Read-only interrupted observation with no record can explicitly repeat.

F. Stable metadata versus freshness. Existing stagedReadSnapshot mixes structural validation with expires>Now+5sec. title: Design a concrete owned-local candidate preparation orchestration
description: Bounded read-only design of smallest actual native candidate-preparation executable/bridge using accepted Worker APIs, retained private desired inputs and canonical receipts. Return Prepared/Waiting/Failed/Unknown with PromotionNotAuthorized only. Explicit pinned pre-existing SA/prerequisites allowed. design:
Recommended first implementation: a concrete process-local candidate-preparation bridge, NOT a new generic engine. Add one small internal/candidateprep package plus an explicitly local command/supervisor (suggest cmd/registry-candidate-local). One accepted project/attempt, one selected ordinary Deployment plus selector-based single-stack ClusterIP Service. It composes accepted runtimeconfig APIs and original private input storage. Public result is Prepared/Waiting/Failed/Unknown with constant PromotionNotAuthorized. It never returns rollout.Succeeded, serving-ready, Pod payload/origin verification, network/HTTP readiness, traffic authority or whole RenderCandidate-bundle parity.

Evidence: runtimeconfig/worker.go:35-110 opens exact pinned subject/owner/cluster/cell and preflights before conditional admission. :113-190 reconstructs already committed D/S from original inputs and independently observes canonical records before any clean successor claim. :191-247 rejects unresolved Pending/Unknown, verifies writer owner/epoch/expiry and exact Gate snapshot; all managed mutations use one Worker. namespace.go:73-84 separates EnsureNamespace (pending before create/UID acknowledgement) from ObserveNamespace (no reservation/create). deployment.go:84-93 and :125-215 retain original bodies before Pending, construct concrete private journal guard, ACK native UID/RV before separate GET, and committed replay only observes. service.go:64-72 and :102-188 similarly require retained Service body and canonical allocation-spec receipt. retirement.go:39-54 blocks new normal mutation after a retained operation fault but permits observation only when no draining attempt. The single desired-runtime declaration is rollout.Desired (rollout/types.go:13-25); journal.DesiredDigest at journal.go:688-690 hashes that safe declaration, NOT private rendered bodies.

Narrow selection/accepted-plan binding: trusted local supervisor accepts and freezes ONE canonical raw Document (project.Prepare validation boundary), exact resolved image provenance/bindings, selection/component and render-contract version, complete private runtime profile and rollout.Desired identity before the first namespace attempt. Derive/bind the runtime revision/reconcile identity to that complete accepted private plan, not merely source branch/image tag. Identity or a digest is not self-authentication; approval comes from concrete trusted bootstrap/acceptance. Preserve raw authoring vs Effective type boundary and never re-normalize an Effective object as raw. After canonical namespace UID exists, render with that same accepted raw Document, exact revision/OperationID and verified NamespacedContext. Both D/S intents, fingerprints and input Targets must equal the same subject/cell/accepted attempt/revision/DesiredDigest/parent UID; verify their logical selectors/ports pair correctly. Worker retains each complete body/ref before the corresponding Pending; each fresh child must resolve those exact refs. A matching DesiredDigest alone cannot authenticate arbitrary private child bodies sharing a revision. Keep the original frozen private accepted plan in the still-live trusted supervisor, copied over bounded private IPC to each child. Loss/change of supervisor plan or pins fails closed; do not reconstruct missing accepted input from live objects/current authoring. Durable production accepted-plan backend stays .5.9; no new general store needed for this controlled first proof. Raw plan/bodies/authentication/checkpoint stay out of stdout/log/history/public diagnostics.

Full-bundle honesty: renderer/core.go:16-32 validates raw authoring; :82-90 always emits empty tenant Role and platform metadata ConfigMap; :105-124 emits component SA/RoleBinding; :131-150 builds ordinary Deployment; Service follows at196+. Runtime supports Namespace/ConfigMap/Deployment/Service, not typed SA/RBAC or every advanced bundle kind. First bridge explicitly selects the D/S pair and declares its prerequisite scope; it must reject an unexpected/unsupported selected workload or required Secret/config input, not silently advertise complete bundle apply. Start with one literal-only ordinary component, digest-pinned image, no dynamic Secret/envFrom/volume/sidecar/worker/HPA/ingress execution. The renderer may describe deferred promotion, but the bridge never calls RenderPromotion or a route writer. Additional rendered infrastructure is either explicitly externally bootstrapped under an independent pin or excluded from the named D/S-preparation claim; don't pretend ignored objects were applied.

Two-phase prerequisite bootstrap: a unique per-attempt namespace cannot already contain the SA before it exists. Phase0 owned fixture supervisor/administrator creates and pins project/control journal and private input store, runs one Worker child to EnsureNamespace with the full accepted desired/attempt, obtains clean Ready checkpoint, and actually waits/reaps that child. The explicitly separate trusted fixture administrator then creates the dedicated SA (and declared supporting fixture prerequisites if needed) in that exact namespace and records actual canonical UID/version/parent/spec facts from its native result. Phase1 clean successor re-observes namespace and exact pre-pinned prerequisites before D/S writes; missing/wrong/replaced parent/SA, false-automount violation or pull-secret injection fails before child mutation. No lookup-by-name adoption and no bootstrap source claiming receipt from a GET. This administrator step is a deliberate owned-fixture bootstrap seam, not a generic runtime mutation API or production privilege recipe. A small concrete read-only prerequisite verifier may be necessary; its injected interface is not proof unless actual owned read/UID/spec evidence backs it. Future typed SA/RBAC capabilities can remove this precondition separately without blocking a working local D/S slice.

Core flow in one admitted child: open once (OpenInitial only empty bootstrap, otherwise OpenClean exact supervisor checkpoint); use EnsureNamespace only in phase0, ObserveNamespace for existing Phase1; bind original accepted plan and verify pinned prerequisites; render/select/freeze pair; ApplyService then ApplyDeployment (both ACK exact private input and native creation receipts before later observation); then bounded paced ObserveService/ObserveDeployment using the accepted original desired bodies/refs. Apply committed replay already observes, but subsequent readiness checks should explicitly call Observe APIs, not indiscriminately run mutation steps on a timer. Stop further mutation after any fault; inspect only via existing permitted reads. Recheck canonical namespace/prerequisite/pair identities at completion; sample window is not an atomic cross-resource or future guarantee.

Prepared means both exact D/S writes are independently committed with canonical receipts and retained original inputs, Service allocation-spec receipt still validates and separately observed Deployment generation/replicas/readiness is Ready. It does not mean endpoints exist, traffic arrives, a Pod runs the approved payload, the image actually executed or promotion is authorized. Waiting means a valid current read returned nonconverged readiness and there is no unresolved write; a bounded observation deadline/observation-count cap returns Waiting, not fabricated failure/retry scheduling. Failed means a known finite input/prerequisite/ownership/rejection/readiness/observation failure is intelligibly retained. A known successful POST followed by GET403/404 remains Committed/Applied internally and Failed observation externally, with original fault and later warnings preserved, no repeated POST. Unknown means provider/write/journal acknowledgement or valid readiness evidence is unresolved/unproven; do not convert it to success/rejection or retry by name. Invalid/future readiness generations/conditions => Unknown; terminating observed resource cannot be Prepared.

Required finite readiness handling: providers/kubernetes/deployment_readiness.go:26-79 returns a successfully read receipt whose Readiness.State can be Failed (ReplicaFailure or ProgressDeadlineExceeded), Waiting, Retained or Unknown. Therefore nil error is NOT Prepared. Current runtimeconfig simply returns this receipt; it does not automatically persist a domain failure for State=Failed. Add a narrowly typed Worker-owned observation-result-to-fault helper/factory, called inside its validated canonical observation path, to map ONLY exact supported readiness failure codes to fixed safe cause/step/action and persist through existing projectFault/commit behavior. Never copy condition Reason/Message or expose a generic Gate/projection publisher. Invalid/unrecognized condition cannot invent Failed or committed mutation facts. If projection ACK is uncertain, retain the same original readiness cause plus independent unknown delivery and stop writes. This helper is part of the subsequent bounded implementation acceptance, not implemented here. Existing API/provider errors already use runtimefault and preserve primary/warnings.

Result/control separation: small safe PreparationResult contains accepted diagnostics.Identity, fixed scope/phase/state/code, constant promotion=NotAuthorized, bounded sample times, reviewed readiness counts and optional existing strict runtimefault.Outcome; no raw DesiredObject, SDK status messages, private refs/paths, addresses/credentials or checkpoint. Receipt-known/prepared observations are descriptive facts, not a write grant. Handoff delivery is an independent PRIVATE supervisor control outcome: a prepared resource result must not be relabeled as physically unknown solely because clean Ready acknowledgement failed, and a Failed cause must not be replaced by shutdown error. Conversely unresolved D/S native receipt acknowledgement makes preparation Unknown. Never expose a boolean supplied by a DTO as proof of process exit.

Process/handoff boundary: Worker.Quiesce worker.go:314-347 closes under its mutex, drains lifecycle unresolved writes and ACKs admission.Ready; RecoverQuiesce :350-372 acknowledges only this same closed actor's retained exact journal/Ready proposal. admission/admission.go:1-4 and :43-48 explicitly deny process-death detection/distributed lock/RPC fencing; BeginResume consumes exact Ready cell version/digest/session once. Supervisor receives checkpoint+private store/cell/plan pins over its bounded owned IPC, keeps them private, and may start successor ONLY after actual owned exec.Cmd.Wait reports the old child exited/reaped. A checkpoint/lease/heartbeat/Temporal activity completion is not exit evidence. Existing integration/runtime_private_helpers_test.go:90-124 uses a bounded private input/result and synchronous CombinedOutput (actual wait/reap); zz_runtime_admission_test.go:69-106 explicitly holds child, Waits and verifies ProcessState. Reuse this finite pattern rather than a new actor framework, arbitrary process command or PID-only reuse.

Cancel/unknown rules: supervisor requests graceful stop/drain first; use a separate fresh bounded shutdown context for Quiesce rather than the already canceled work context. If Ready ACK is uncertain, only same still-owned closed child may perform exact RecoverQuiesce; no provider retry or reopening. If child dies/loses IPC before confirmed clean handoff, hangs, is killed, or has unresolved native writes, do not mint checkpoint or start a fresh writer from observed process death. Report retained/unknown and leave exact evidence. Fresh-process recovery of an ambiguous provider write remains unsupported children .5.1.2/.5.5.2. Clean preflight failure does not consume checkpoint; after that failed child actually exits a supervisor may retry the same read-only preflight against unchanged pins when an external issue is repaired, never bypass it.

Coordinator boundary: existing coordinator/activities.go:15-53 constructs a NewEngine/Stepper per activity and workflow.go:195 configures automatic activity retries; those abstractions are not a native Worker lifetime or distributed fencing. First real executable is the supervised local child orchestration only, without adapting native refs into simulation Candidate/Route aliases, registering a production Temporal worker, caching an actor in activity memory or assuming one Temporal workflow prevents duplicate live activity processes. A later explicit PrepareCandidate activity may return the safe result and address the already-owned supervisor through a reviewed channel; it may not start/admit another actor just because Temporal retries. Failure/unknown outcomes must remain blocked until actual exact recovery; Prepared must not masquerade as full RolloutSucceeded.

Exact next proof matrix: (1) real owned API success using one accepted plan, exact native immutable image and pinned SA; one D/S POST each, retained refs survive independent reopen, fresh Ready/allocated reads => Prepared+PromotionNotAuthorized, no route/traffic call. (2) same accepted identity across namespace setup then Wait/reap and successor apply; observed current UIDs/spec fingerprints/Service digest remain; another clean successor performs only GET and no second POST. (3) known readiness failure from actual controlled failing workload yields safe finite Failed cause despite nil API error, persists cause after writer exit and never Prepared or deletes candidate. (4) POST known result ACKed before injected403/404 read failure remains canonical committed; exact cause/independent later warning retained; successor inspection uses original private source and no POST replay. (5) missing/tampered private body, changed accepted plan/revision/UID/SA, stale or copied checkpoint and concurrent successor attempts fail before new child writes. (6) lost provider response or unknown native/journal ACK forbids successor/handoff/replay; no absence/name proof. (7) actual held old process proves supervisor does not launch successor before Wait, even if Ready bytes arrived; cancellation with no confirmed Ready is retained/unknown. Pure sequencing fakes may check call order but cannot replace native process/API proof. No tests/API runs/source edits in this design.
acceptance_criteria: Concrete finite orchestration seam reuses accepted primitives without simulation aliases or broad abstractions, specifies exact accepted-input/prerequisite authority, process ownership and clean restart protocol, and meaningful actual success/failure/unknown/restart evidence. Root reviews bounded design; implementation/native proof/promotion remain open.

title: Design fresh durable auth-only candidate observation receipt policy
description: Root requests concrete next bounded proposal after actual actorTLS acceptance. Specify fresh policy/schema and immutable activity-local auth-only observation receipt persistence using the validated Observer contract and private Staged read guard. Existing staging-only intent/policy/registry/localmetadata semantics must not be reinterpreted, and current observational DTO must not satisfy manager Verified, workflow/worker readiness, activation or cleanup. Design exact receipt binding/CAS/unknown/restart semantics and negative tests; no source, tests, cloud or credential work until root review.
design:
REVISED TERMINAL-ONLY AUTH-OBSERVATION RECEIPT LANE (root challenge accepted; supersedes pre-TLS Requested proposal in historical notes). Design only; no implementation before concrete root review.

1. Existing immutable policies/APIs remain exact. DisposableRetainOnFailure still means Staged terminal/no Verified/cleanup. ObserveStaged remains stateless and never appends receipt/history. New optional AuthObservationPolicy in localmetadata.Config enables only Actor.RecordAuthObservation, a local diagnostic metadata recording operation. This is NOT a new CredentialFailurePolicy, VerifyCandidates, CanaryAttestation/Passed, activation or consumer readiness. Scope remains disposable/preprovisioned-SA/create-SA-off/short TTL, no revoke/delete/workflow writes/cloud mutation. The existing validated credentialobservation.Contract remains the only evidence meaning.

2. Reuse one localmetadata root/lock/append/commit/uncertainty machinery as THIRD independent typed channel. Add AuthObservations handle/map and optional AuthObservation pointer at END of frame+Revision with json omitempty. Receipt append changes global sequence/history only; per-Journal and per-Outcome versions remain unchanged. Zero policy keeps EXACT existing configDigest struct branch, identity/intent/commit schemas, frame bytes and checkpoint Schema1; no added null/default fields. Nonzero policy uses fresh explicit identity/intent/commit schemas and versioned configDigest envelope containing old base config digest+policy. New/old schema interchange rejected. Fresh empty directory/bootstrapUID/inode binding ONLY, no migration/import/copy/reinterpretation. Registry adds omitted-zero AuthObservationPolicyDigest and selects new receipt schema only alongside exact existing ObservationBindingDigest. Receipt-enabled checkpoint Schema2 includes exact policy digest; old zero remains exact Schema1 bytes. OpenClean cross-checks all bindings. All new receipt frames enter existing global history/count/digest clean-handoff witness.

3. Policy fields: Contract=temporal-candidate-auth-observation-receipt-v1; ObservationContract exactly credentialobservation.Contract; ObservationBindingDigest exactly actor trusted settings+KMS fingerprint; max terminal receipts per stage bounded1..8. Existing global MaximumRevisions/MaximumRecordBytes still apply. No key/material/client/maps/raw provider versions in policy/records. ReaderBindingID is trusted bootstrap provenance, never SDK/IAM permission proof. No separate companion filesystem backend or duplicated CAS implementation.

4. Typed terminal receipt: Schema/Contract/ID/Version, explicit hex64 caller-persisted AttemptID, immutable expected refs (owner, namespace ID/birth/incarnation, slot/stage/credential attempt/write/candidate store+canonical ARN/resource birth, SA/key identities, exact credential Journal+Outcome versions, actor binding digest), actor provenance (trusted ControlCellUID, hash of raw cell version, admission generation/sessionID, writerID/epoch), RecordedAt, Kind=Observed OR NotEstablished, and exactly one safe Observation or finite failure. RecordID=hash(policy+owner/slot+AttemptID); never derives from varying result/time or silently rebinds same AttemptID. Map/tombstone makes AttemptID immutable store-wide. This provenance is not a capability, cryptographic network attestation or proof against malicious os.Root holder. Canonical provider IDs remain existing trusted reference contract; only version digests persist.

5. One transition only: ABSENT -> TERMINAL, after actual observation completes. NO Requested phase, NO durable pre-read intent, NO logical pending-read blocker. A lost read result without any receipt may be explicitly read again safely; exact-once network/read claims are forbidden. Existing terminal match returns Historical=true without TLS/secret fetch, never claims freshness. Same AttemptID with changed input or result cannot overwrite/rebind; a separately explicit new AttemptID may record a later observation within bounded capacity. Terminal CAS is insert-only expected absence; exact retry can return identical accepted receipt, differing proposal conflicts. A successful receipt embeds exact safe Observer.Observation incl schema/contract, IDs/owner/stage/write/version refs, endpoint digest, provider-version digests and start/completion/expiry; validate against exact Staged+MetadataVerified state and public policy, bounded times/expiry. An observed ACTIVE digest is evidence only; staged KeyRef/phase never refresh and receipt is not revocation precondition. NotEstablished stores only whitelisted Observer Code+Step and no Observation. No raw SDK/errors/headers/native versions/key values. It is historical failure of finite auth observation, not a general candidate-health blame.

6. Actor sequence: hold existing mu+registry lock; validate current authority/namespace/settings+paired exact Staged/Outcome metadata; capture immutable expected refs; find existing terminal AttemptID and return explicitly historical only when exact inputs match; preflight bounded receipt capacity BEFORE TLS without persisting anything. Invoke existing private actual Observer.New/read guard exactly as accepted (no recursive public ObserveStaged lock, no broader create CandidateGuard, no fake/raw exports). After return candidate material and connections are closed, then recheck exact authority/session/writer and unchanged credential/outcome refs before inserting one terminal receipt via third channel. Observer/private read guard remains unchanged in authority/phase meaning; no own-Requested exception is needed. If metadata or authority changed, return finite original/local failure and no fabricated record. Stateless ObserveStaged receives NO new receipt-phase gate.

7. Persistence uncertainty: terminal append/CAS/fsync/readback ambiguity returns zero acknowledged receipt plus finite ReceiptOutcomeUnknown; retain exact AttemptID/request/proposed receipt digest and original finite observation failure separately if known. Existing localmetadata sticky uncertainty, pending exact-frame recovery, no reset/prune and unknown handoff denial remain unchanged. Never infer absent receipt means provider noncall, succeeded read, freshness or failed authentication. A canceled/deadline context may prevent terminal append: report no receipt acknowledgment; do not use background authority to manufacture one. With no append attempted/receipt present, a separate explicit read remains safe. If the shared substrate itself is uncertain, its existing integrity gates apply; no new bypass that treats underlying journal/outcome facts as proven. Existing bounded exact pending-frame recovery may acknowledge the exact terminal record, not invent a lost network result or replay unsafe provider mutation. Historical receipt stays historical after restart/expiry, never promotion authorization. Rollback/high-water .9.6.3 remains open; no distributed/external-writer/provider-finality guarantee.

8. Acceptance: exact old-zero config/identity/frame/history/checkpoint bytes; fresh/new-old schema/config/binding/checkpoint mismatch; independent third-channel versions; insert-only duplicate vs changed attempt/input/result; finite contracts/codes/steps and no mutable frames; foreign stage/write/owner/ARN/resource birth/version/settings/session evidence denied; stale/expired proof; observed version bump recorded only as fact while staged state unchanged; capacity preflight no TLS; interrupted read without record can separately rerun; append-after-intent/commit/fsync faults sticky+exact recovery; concurrent opens/CAS; no raw token sentinel in any durable frame/JSON/fmt/errors. Actor positive proof must use public ctor/private actual Observer.New+actual generated local TLS in owned scratch tier, no fake observer injection. Extend finite actor tagged selection for terminal success, foreign identity failure, exact replay no extra calls, clean handoff and uncertain receipt append retaining stage. Default tests no network/exec; NEVER host-run tag. Proposed split: backend/schema+negative/fault tests child first; actor Record integration+ownedTLS child second. No module/common journal/provider/cloud changes.
acceptance_criteria: Exact typed policy/schema and receipt identity/order/unknown semantics recorded with repository evidence and upgrade limits; clear boundary to future manager auth-only verification, promotion and consumer readiness; root decision before source implementation.
notes: DESIGN SELF-REVIEW CLARIFICATIONS before root review: ObservationAttemptID must have a store-wide immutable tombstone mapping to its derived RecordID, so changing journal/outcome refs cannot turn one caller attempt ID into another record. Global unresolved Requested blocks ordinary public ObserveStaged/Advance/Quiesce/new Record requests. Only the exact live private Record invocation may let its own matching committed Requested record pass the private read snapshot/guard; this must be an unexported capability pinned to exact receipt Version/session and at-most-once callback, not a generic ignore-pending flag. Common public historySafe remains strict. Store terminal validation checks current exact Staged+Outcome refs and immutable Requested input, actual actor admission remains the authority boundary; ledger syntax is not proof a network call occurred. Terminal failure codes/steps are closed whitelist; malformed/typednil/unrecognized errors become one finite Unknown observation failure only if live authority+safe terminal persistence remain established, otherwise Requested retained.
close_reason: Root accepted revised terminal-only post-read auth receipt design: no Requested gate/replay/freshness claim; fresh integrated schema and independent channel versions; historical stable refs separate from current authority and expired history structurally readable. Backend and actor composition follow in separate implementation children.

title: Sequence an owned-local authenticated diagnostic browser slice
description: Bounded read-only sequencing/design review of canonical diagnostic browser discovery and provider-native rollout composition. Propose smallest same-origin owned-local page/server using real durable journal, explicit canonical bootstrap Target, existing session/live policy readers and existing JS panel. No source edits, tests, cloud/API run or live legacy route changes in this design child.
design:
Sequencing recommendation: implement one owned-local, read-only diagnostic browser vertical slice FIRST. It uses an already persisted real runtime fault, survives the worker process exiting, and renders actionable cause/recovery/delivery/freshness through the existing schema and panel. It does not depend on Pod declaration/profile work, unknown-create recovery, a native rollout Stepper, route promotion, cloud/build parity or a production web deployment.

Evidence: resources.py:4086-4143 emits name/catalog-status file key, no canonical project UID/environment/installation/diagnostic enablement; server.py:250-262 overlays raw status, and :1274-1277 exposes registry/catalog routes without per-project diagnostic policy there (this is route-level code, not proof of ingress exposure). app.js:229-263 uses project.name as drawer id and drops status/scope; :290-299 fetches /api/registry; :1085-1114 replaces/removes drawer DOM and clears workspace timers only. Do not switch fetch to /api/catalog or add raw status to the panel. catalogdiagnostics/http.go already supplies fixed same-origin per-UID GET/HEAD, no-store/private and exact server-side scope. Model.Read checks live grant before/after source; JournalSource has exact pinned source and independent desired observation. project_policy.go NewPinnedReadPolicy/CheckDiagnosticRead is a concrete current owned policy ConfigMap reader, not default employee authorization. diagnostics.mjs:187-230 already implements trusted binding, no construction-time fetch, exact relative endpoint, same-origin/no-store/no redirects, bounded JSON, abort/generation clearing and destroy. registry-operator-demo currently runs only simulation; no real runtime executable is implied by that command.

Bounded server/common seam (root-owned): add a separate explicitly local diagnostic page/server with a SINGLE immutable trusted bootstrap binding {Enabled, Target, pinned Repository/Journal identity, pinned Desired cell, pinned Policy cell, origin/optional operationID}. Target is exact accepted fixture subject Environment/Installation/ProjectUID from independently trusted bootstrap; validate matching journal Subject and policy/desired Target plus canonical cell/namespace UIDs. Display names are presentation only. No catalog name, file key, Temporal namespace, authoring flag, URL/header environment or live descendant body can select this binding. A UID string or digest does not authenticate itself; root must bind the concrete existing source readers and explicit trusted bootstrap. Existing owned fixture ProjectUID is an accepted bootstrap identity; this slice does not pretend it has proved mapping from a production DemoProject CR metadata.uid. Actual canonical catalog discovery remains parent-open.

Local registration: explicitly enabled fixture-only page at a separate fixed path, static assets from an exact allowlist, one bounded same-origin binding route (proposed GET /api/v2/diagnostics/binding), existing GET /api/v2/projects/{UID}/diagnostics handler. Binding endpoint authorizes the fixed configured Target with actual SessionAuthorizer/current PinnedReadPolicy before exposing Target/enabled/project binding, then rechecks before response; unauthenticated requests do not perform journal/existence reads, forbidden is indistinguishable from absent. Disabled default registers no diagnostic discovery/reads and makes no request. Generic HTML shell need contain no target or protected data; bootstrap is fetched only after explicit user click. Return only existing panel binding shape {enabled:true,target:Target} in bounded metadata JSON, not a second diagnostic view schema. No arbitrary source selection/list endpoint, no stored private filesystem/provider locator, no worker query/mutation/recovery callback. Use explicit owned listener/TLS identity; no ambient config or production registration.

Authentication claims: browser receives an independently minted owned fixture session cookie matching the exact existing legacy HMAC claim profile, and the REAL SessionAuthorizer validates signature/issuer/audience/time/domain/subject and the REAL pinned live per-project policy reader. The fixture issuer/session is SYNTHETIC issuance and does not prove Google OAuth/login integration, production session-key delivery, ingress auth, existing catalog authorization or production discovery. Existing route cannot authenticate from headers. Owned bootstrap supplies key material explicitly to server, never browser source, argv/logs/history/public config. The browser only holds its scoped HttpOnly cookie. Production issuer/key/bootstrap/ingress/session registration remain .13.3.3 follow-up.

UI seam (agent-owned after scope approval/freeze release): one new small opt-in page adapter with mount/destroy/clear and explicit Load/Refresh, reusing mountDiagnosticPanel and existing normalize/render logic. The adapter receives only the fixed authorized binding endpoint, bounds/validates its one Target and enabled flag, then mounts the existing panel; it cannot select endpoint URLs, emit rich HTML or persist bindings/views. No changes to live app.js/server.py or new diagnostic schema. Keep no polling. Destroy on close/navigation/pagehide; clear protected data before logout, when hidden or before refresh, and on 401/403/404/invalid/timeout/source unavailable; pageshow from back-forward cache starts empty and requires a fresh authorized load. Generation/AbortController must also cover discovery, so a late response cannot repopulate a closed or replaced page. Cross-scope inputs reject rather than retarget the same mounted controller.

Logout is a browser/server lifecycle seam, not global revocation by cookie deletion. If root adds a fixture logout endpoint, it is fixed same-origin, clears only the correct local cookie and returns no protected data; UI clears BEFORE dispatch. Independently updating policy revokes future/inflight source reads. No promise to remotely erase already seen data or instantly notice remote revocation without polling; this local page clears on explicit refresh/focus/visibility lifecycle and every authorization failure. Tests must distinguish cached DOM retention from server authorization and avoid claiming instantaneous push revocation.

Smallest real proof: one controlled existing runtime fault with actual owned Kubernetes journal storage and private desired input, writer process exited/reaped, then separate read-only server process/handler plus ACTUAL browser load of the real page/module. Root's corrected API5 proves storage/history/native materialization separately; use that same native input/canonical UID/accepted Target rather than hand-writing a failure DTO. Live policy is the real owned mutable policy cell; fixture session is synthetic-minted but cryptographically verified. Browser sees fixed original cause and NextAction, distinct cleanup/evidence/publication if present, known Applied versus observation failure where appropriate, route Unconfirmed/retry Unknown, independent desired/progress/read timestamps, unknown persistence time/Partial. No raw values, private paths, session/key, provider messages or locator links in DOM/network payload/screenshot. Do not fabricate recovery states just to make one screenshot richer; cover optional scenarios in existing pure panel/model tests and a second explicit fixture only when needed.

Proof tier: first pure adapter/Go binding route tests with injected fake DOM/fetch are labeled contract-only; then acquire an explicitly pinned official browser/tool artifact under separate reviewed acquisition, and execute a finite owned isolated browser/server test with no host credentials, no Docker socket inside, no default external route, bounded public asset input and owned cleanup. Browser gets no Kubernetes client credentials; server alone has explicit read-only fixture bootstrap. Trust owned TLS via exact local CA/trust material rather than global certificate-error bypass. No generic browser endpoint override or network route interception faking the diagnostic API. Root/local_testing must review artifact pin, boundary and resources before running; do not reuse Node16 fake DOM as a claim of actual browser proof.

Finite acceptance for this slice: default disabled/no diagnostic fetch; valid fixture cookie + real live policy + exact Target reads existing durable failure after writer exit; anonymous/header-only and foreign UID/scope denied before JournalSource; same-origin/no-store response and no redirects; actual DOM displays correct current wire fields and text-escapes injected fixture text; refresh after real policy revocation clears prior cause and cannot publish a delayed authorized response after revocation/close; logout/pagehide/back-forward restoration starts empty; source unavailable versus authorized NotObserved/absence stay truthful; exactly owned browser/server/network resources cleaned and no skipped exact cases. Actual browser test need not exercise every broad catalog/parity case to close its bounded child; parent still carries production discovery/legacy drawer integration.

Provider-native rollout sequencing: do not force existing engine/simulation resource aliases into native runtime or equate Endpoint publication with promotion. runtimeconfig currently offers separate Ensure/ObserveNamespace, Apply/ObserveDeployment and Service with retained private inputs/canonical receipts; these can produce reportable failure without any traffic route. Next native orchestration milestone, if selected later, should be an explicit candidate-preparation result (Prepared/Waiting/Failed/Unknown, PromotionNotAuthorized) that composes ONLY available typed capabilities under the actual accepted attempt and returns safe Outcome; it is not RolloutSucceeded or serving-ready. Dedicated SA/prerequisites currently appear as explicit fixture-admin bootstrap in native API proofs, so a real generic candidate executable must either require independently pinned pre-existing prerequisites or add their bounded typed adapters first. Unknown writes remain blocked; no generic retry/adoption. Automatic routing waits for separate route CAS authority plus reviewed declaration/trust/smoke composition. A useful diagnostic page can ship before that entire native actor exists.

Suggested durable split: root server/common bootstrap + authorized single-binding route; agent new standalone page adapter/pure tests; local_testing reviewed real browser isolated tier/native proof; later production catalog publisher actual UID discovery/retired mapping + opt-in drawer lifecycle + session/ingress registration. No implementation performed in this review; all sources remain frozen through current API5 and default aggregate.

title: Specify pinned current ReplicaSet and Pod API payload equivalence contract
description: Read-only design audit for a separate pinned Kubernetes v1.37 current RS/Pod API payload-equivalence capability against independently retained original Deployment. Inventory actual renderer/provider baseline and reviewed controller/admission/scheduler deltas, explicit unsupported cases and safe source seams. Keep Secret/ConfigMap incarnation/content-consumption evidence, node-placement/runtime image limits, creator origin and promotion authorization separate. No provider/common source edits, network/API run or implementation in this design child.
design:
Proposed first capability: current_workload_api_declaration_v1, pinned to the reviewed Kubernetes v1.37.0 server/controller build and k8s.io/api v0.37.0. It verifies the CURRENT API-declared ReplicaSet template and Pod spec against independently retained accepted Deployment input. It does not verify process argv/env/files, consumed dependency contents, image execution, creator origin, node trust, DNS/packets/HTTP or promotion authority. This is useful under an explicitly trusted managed cluster and is deliberately narrower than the parent implementation acceptance.

Repository inventory (current lines): providers/kubernetes/deployment_defaults.go:17-23 documents closed typed v1.37 full-spec comparison, no DeepDerivative or unreviewed Pod-only defaults. Lines43-62 allow exactly one container, named SA, automount=false, empty Pod security context, CPU/memory resources; lines64-96 allow TCP ports/readiness and env refs but reject every Pod/container field outside the complete typed whitelist. Lines100-178 normalize the existing Deployment template defaults. render/kubernetes/core.go:97-150 renders digest images, one main container, command/args/env/resources/TCP ports/readiness, named SA, DNSConfig and ownership labels. render/kubernetes/pod_features.go:22-105 can ALSO render exec liveness, sidecar and Secret volumes; those do not satisfy today's provider baseline and are explicitly unsupported here. environment.go:86-163 can inject Secret refs/envFrom and thus many worker configurations do not satisfy the proposed literal-only slice. types.go:18 SecretBinding pins namespace UID/owner/name/keys, not Secret object UID/version/immutability. endpoint_verify.go:125-165 verifies ancestry/selectors/labels but not RS template or Pod spec. runtimeinputs/types.go:56-66,94-106 retains original Deployment privately under accepted Target and returns only copied execution data. DeploymentRead at deployment_types.go:85-93 plus independent canonical record is the proper source seam, not DeploymentView/creation RV as authority; ObserveDeployment performs fresh full-spec validation. Existing EndpointRead:12-22 correctly calls out actor responsibility to resolve accepted private inputs/receipts.

Inputs: freeze the original retained Deployment body and accepted InputReference/Target (exact subject, cellUID, accepted desired digest/revision/attempt, namespace UID, child fingerprint, canonical Deployment UID); resolve from the real admitted journal/private store, not current project authoring, labels, a public readiness DTO, or observed descendants. Run the existing full-spec ObserveDeployment before enumeration and again at completion. Proposed private PayloadRead carries DeploymentRead, independently trusted ReviewedClusterProfile capability and finite limits. A freely constructible profile hash is descriptive, never evidence of installed configuration. Retained request bodies remain private/opaque under JSON/fmt and copied before callbacks. No mutation callbacks or write permission in the reader.

First supported subset: ordinary one-container Deployment satisfying the existing closed provider whitelist, immutable digest image declaration, literal Env values only (no ValueFrom/EnvFrom), no volumes/init/ephemeral/sidecar containers, no container or Pod security extensions, automount explicitly false, named dedicated SA, no imagePullSecrets, no template annotations, ordinary default scheduler and no author-specified node placement/priority/runtimeClass/affinity/tolerations/topology or resource claims. Keep exact authored array ordering and explicit pointer presence as pinned wire normalization requires. Literal $ expansion is left exactly as authored; equality does not prove kubelet-resolved process values, image ENTRYPOINT/CMD/env defaults, or service-injected variables. CPU/memory limits/requests and TCP readiness/DNSConfig remain useful supported literals.

Expected RS: derive from independently normalized retained Deployment.Spec.Template, never RS-observed spec. Require exact full template equality after adding only one bounded pod-template-hash LABEL consistently to RS selector, RS template and Pod labels; do not delete arbitrary labels or annotations. Validate canonical RS UID/RV/namespace, exactly one controllerRef to canonical Deployment UID/name, expected match-label selector, and MinReadySeconds. Hash consistency establishes a controller-shaped declaration, not its creator, and cannot bypass payload comparison. Controller replicas are a separately changing scaling field: this reader does not claim full ReplicaSet scaling/status equivalence or readiness. RS metadata envelope/status are classified explicitly rather than silently dropped from an alleged whole-object comparison; native generated name/timestamps/managedFields/controller revision counters are not template payload. Unknown annotations/finalizers or behavioral metadata remain unsupported in the first profile. Adoption of an identical payload may satisfy this CURRENT declaration claim; adopted or mutated nonmatching payload fails even when labels/owner chain match.

Expected Pod: construct from the retained normalized template plus the finite profile transformations, then compare the ENTIRE typed v1.37 PodSpec. Finite candidate deltas are: enableServiceLinks=true when omitted; each missing CPU/memory request copies that resource's explicit limit; exact Priority admission no-default-class result (priority0, empty class, preemptLowerPriority); exact two DefaultTolerationSeconds entries from reviewed configuration, no extra tolerations; NodeName empty or one syntactically valid scheduler assignment under the separately stated trusted scheduler assumption. The NodeName delta must be explicit output AssignmentObserved/PlacementUnverified, not silently strip nodeName and claim full desired placement. Dedicated SA has no imagePullSecrets, token automount=false, so injected pull secrets/token volumes are unexpected. Pod-level resources stay nil; pinned helper returns without changing absent pod-level resource object. No automatic allowances for LimitRange, mutating webhooks, custom scheduler binding labels/annotations or security injection. Template-normalized container/pod defaults are reused exactly, not repeatedly generalized. Every other typed spec field must match expected zero/value; unexpected feature/default yields UnsupportedProfile or PayloadMismatch.

Pod metadata: exact expected labels (including only consistent hash), empty annotations/finalizers in first profile, namespace/UID/RV/name validity, exactly one controllerRef to verified RS UID/name with pinned controller flags; deletion/termination or changed generation causes Waiting/Changed rather than an enduring verification result. Generated name/server timestamps/managedFields are server metadata, not app payload; they are separately bounded and never used as birth provenance. Pod status/readiness and running imageID are not payload proof and do not replace separate readiness capability. Unknown typed fields fail closed; official SDK decoding can discard unknown future wire fields, so this is a trusted pinned v1.37 server contract, not a generic future-schema strict decoder.

Enumeration/freshness: reuse bounded consistent pagination pattern from Endpoint observer (default16/page, at most8 pages,128 Pods,16 RS,2MiB postdecode and10s; hard ceilings remain finite), list all relevant selector/owned descendants rather than cherry-pick a good Pod, reject duplicate-name/differentUID or inconsistent duplicate bodies/page RV/continue-token cycles, and mark incomplete on bound or source error. Both foreign selector matches and unexpected owned descendants prevent an aggregate Equivalent claim. No Pods is Waiting, not vacuous Verified. End re-read namespace canonical UID, exact Deployment spec/generation, and relevant RS/Pod UID+spec+label/annotation/owner digests; changes produce Changed/Incomplete. Stable rechecks bound an observed interval, not an atomic multi-resource snapshot, permanent fence, proof of no intervening transient change or future guarantee. Postdecode byte budget is not a proof of hostile decoder allocation bounds.

Output: opaque snapshot with fixed version/claim/code, Equivalent/Waiting/Mismatch/Unsupported/Incomplete state, counts, accepted fingerprint, namespace/Deployment UID/generation and sample interval/digest. Export no Pod body/addresses/env/image strings/raw annotations/errors/private source locators. A finite mismatch field category may be exposed without values. Payload declaration equality and completeness are distinct; creatorOriginVerified=false, processValuesVerified=false, promotionAuthorized=false. Public JSON cannot be reconstructed into an execution grant. Future endpoint composition must correlate the SAME private canonical Pod UID set and accepted deployment/namespace identity; public counts and coincident timestamps are insufficient.
