title: Specify actor-private staged observation guard and immutable read binding
description: Root requests bounded read-only proposal before any frozen actor edits. Compose actual credentialobservation.New privately under actor lifecycle/registry/admission, exact staged state/outcome and namespace birth, no manager verification/cleanup/phase changes. Bind observation endpoints/public trust/project/reader scope immutably across clean handoff; reject caller auth/routing before any pre-read. Reuse finite owned local TLS opt-in tier for actual composition proof, no exported fake/raw-token or shared Gate/permit factories. Identify fresh-bootstrap/compatibility limits honestly. No source/module/cloud changes during this design task.
design:
READ-ONLY .6.5 PROPOSAL (2026-10-30), no actor/source/module/cloud edits or heavy checks. Root accepted/closed nativearm64 isolated wire .4.1/.4.1.1; standalone .6.4 remains open for fresh default aggregate (now10 default tests, added ignored-version-date regression). This design must be reviewed before frozen actor changes.

BOUNDED API / CONSTRUCTION:
Keep actor mode disposable/local/staging-only and manager policy exactly unchanged: StageAPIKeys true, VerifyCandidates/Revoke/CreateSA false, preprovisioned SA, TTL<=1h. Add optional trusted ObservationRuntime to actor Config: public ObservationSettings{ProjectID,TrustBindingID,ReaderBindingID,Cloud/Data explicit public-CA endpoints,ExpectedDataPlaneID,Timeout<=10s} plus separate explicit narrow SecretReader credentialobservation.SecretClient. No injected Observer, Guard, fake probe factory, raw token, generic callback, shared Gate or credential getter in public actor config/API. Nil settings means read capability disabled (explicit finite error). Construct actual credentialobservation.New privately in configureProviders before any admission Claim; its actual read-only localmetadata loaders + unexported actorReadGuard are supplied there. Transfer SecretReader dependency into Observer's opaque private state and retain only copied public settings in stored actor config; do not add a printable raw credential field. New constructor makes no network/key read. Existing staging-only configs remain unchanged.
Public finite method proposal ObserveStaged(ctx, ObserveRequest{StageID,WriteID,CredentialJournalVersion}) -> credentialobservation.Observation,error. All request fields are SHA256 references already returned by Advance; no caller namespace/SA/key/ARN/endpoint or authoring payload. Actor derives its one slot from trusted owner+namespace incarnation, loads exact current Staged record and matches all caller expectations before provider/secret reads. An old request never silently observes another stage. This returns observational diagnostic data only, not manager CanaryAttestation or CredentialVerified.

IMMUTABLE READ AUTHORITY / FRESH BOOTSTRAP LIMIT:
Current registry schema pins owner/control identity/namespace birth/metadata binding/store/inventory but no read endpoints/project/trust/reader binding (registry.go:55-80). Add optional omitted-zero ObservationBindingDigest and an explicit read-enabled schema variant/version. Digest covers public reviewed ObservationSettings PLUS the actor exact KMS ARN/provenance binding, never SDK client/auth material. Existing manifest binds owner/store/namespace/metadata/control provenance but DOES NOT currently pin KMS; read-enabled binding must add it explicitly. The non-authorizing fingerprint helper therefore receives both public settings and the exact trusted KMS binding. A pure non-authorizing ObservationSettingsFingerprint helper can let bootstrap coordinator review/pin settings; it grants no request permission and makes no IAM/principal claim. Actor Open requires exact nil/zero or nonnil/equal digest correspondence (no implicit enable OR disable), and real Observer.New validates copied CA/endpoint/settings before claim.
Use old v1 only for zero read binding, new explicit read-enabled schema for nonzero binding; strict decode, directory/lock/manifest inode+digest and checkpoint RegistryBinding remain unchanged. Therefore old actor fixtures cannot gain observation capability by changing Config, copying manifest or rebuilding a different registry on clean resume. FIRST LANE IS FRESH EXPLICITLY BOOTSTRAPPED READ-ENABLED ACTOR FIXTURES ONLY. No in-place registry upgrade/reset/adoption, alternate checkpoint bypass or mixed-version-resume claim. New read-enabled clean handoff must preserve exact settings digest and registry binding. Role/session credentials are not hashed/persisted; ReaderBindingID is independently reviewed coordinator provenance for the expected dedicated reader, not proof of the actual SDK client's IAM permissions (real effective permission remains .3.3).

READ LIFECYCLE / PRIVATE GUARD:
1. ObserveStaged acquires the same actor.mu as Advance/Quiesce and checks monotone closed BEFORE any registry/Gate I/O. Reject any inherited outgoing auth/reserved routing before ANY namespace pre-read, so the existing namespace adapter cannot borrow an admin header. Drop other outgoing metadata before its scoped pre-read. No public context/permit factory.
2. Hold same registry flock for the WHOLE observation and generated SDK connection close/return. Check registry identity/read binding, actual Gate Snapshot (pinned cell/session/subject/epoch), exact fresh Writer ID/owner/expiry. Validate metadata.History and reject uncertain/unresolved phases; require exact retain-policy Staged state, MetadataVerified matching outcome, expected slot/stage/write/version/candidate/SA/key/birth/receipt and inactive/nonreserved identity from immutable bootstrap inventory. No Active=false shortcut. Existing namespace Adapter.Observe independently verifies exact owned namespace birth/ACTIVE/API-key mode before material access, using only explicit namespace-scoped transport; no creation/adoption/recreation.
3. Mint private per-invocation read capability containing actor identity, active session/epoch/writer, exact namespace birth, Staged reference/state version, Outcome version and safe immutable key/create receipt. Store it only while actor mutex+registry lock are held. Distinct read context key/type from existing namespace/create invocation: create capability cannot authorize read, read cannot authorize create. No reentrant lock: actorReadGuard.Run verifies live exact private invocation/ref, at-most-once callback and independently reloads exact state/outcome/session/registry under already-held lock, then invokes Observer callback directly. It must not acquire actor.mu or flock again. Live capability invalidated on every exit; retained/borrowed contexts deny.
4. Observer performs its existing production exact secret metadata/version/TLS identity/namespace reads and closes clients/material before callback returns. Guard and outer method recheck exact versions, registry, writer/session and namespace binding before releasing. Any failed authority/metadata recheck returns no proof; do not mislabel authority loss as a bad candidate. Public output keeps only finite observation/error fields. Reads cannot commit a credential/Outcome/root-journal revision, refresh a durable key digest, set FailureCode/CleanupFailureCode or call manager Advance/Verify/Revoke/DeleteCandidate.
5. Read failures/cancel/timeouts retain Staged and permit another explicitly bounded fresh diagnostic read; provider reads have no mutation-finality claim. Existing ambiguous create/store/history still blocks reads/new attempts/handoff. Quiesce waits for the whole read/callback/client close by same mutex+flock, then sets its existing monotone closed before I/O; failed/canceled shutdown never reopens dispatch. Clean checkpoint history count/tip remains unchanged by reads and still pins independent high-water. External bypass writers, restored files/crash recovery without witness, distributed/provider fencing and future validity remain unsupported.

ACTUAL COMPOSITION PROOF WITHOUT FAKE/RAW FACTORY EXPORT:
Default tests cover construction/settings digest/disabled/foreign/stale/unknown/closed/ref mismatch and private capability negatives without opening sockets. There must be NO positive default path that injects fake Observer or grants a bypass Guard to make it pass. Positive composition is new tagged actor-package test through public OpenInitial/OpenClean -> actual private Observer.New -> actual generated TLS clients, inside SAME owned scratch/loopback tier as accepted wire proof. Actor's real pinned Cell/Repository/admission, private lifecycle/registry lock and actual localmetadata run with existing owned synchronous Kube/Temporal-create/AWS metadata providers; a test-local secure fake store wrapper copies only synthetic creation material synchronously for exact-version reader. Fake writer/reader dependency remains explicit test-only memory, not production encryption/IAM evidence. No exported token/fake constructor in production packages. Local tagged test file may reuse/duplicate private TLS fixture helpers; reuse the tier/runner contract rather than publishing a raw-token helper API.
Current --credential-observation-wire intentionally selects only the standalone package/top test. Add a SEPARATE finite mutually-exclusive actor-wire mode (for example --credential-staging-observation-wire) with exact package ./internal/credentialstaging, same opt-in tag+owned marker, exact TestActorStagedObservationLocalTLSLifecycle,count1,90s/no fixtures/no skips. Keep accepted standalone/default/metadata selections unchanged; no arbitrary target/tag/env option. Root reviews this runner extension/source snapshot before actual run; NEVER host-run tag.

MINIMUM MEANINGFUL TEST CASES:
- Fresh read-enabled bootstrap stages via actual manager/store/metadata, then actual Observer.New success with wire candidate-only header/route counters; credential phase/version/failure/cleanup, metadata history/tip/files, stage creates/deletes unchanged by both successful and failed observations. Zero secret/material in output/errors/frames.
- Stale caller StageID/write/journal version, non-Staged/uncertain metadata, foreign namespace birth/owner/SA/key, reserved runtime identity, closed/canceled actor or inherited auth/route -> zero secret fetch and no candidate TLS headers. Verify operator namespace pre-read cannot borrow caller authorization.
- Read private capability exact session/epoch/writer/ref/state/outcome mismatch, copied expired invocation, duplicate callback or create/read cross-kind use -> deny before callback (no public permit).
- Actual TLS identity/namespace mismatch and interrupted read retain original Staged record; no compensation/revocation/verification or digest refresh. Existing standalone tests already cover exact reader/trust/refused/budget limits; do not repeat private mechanism claims as wire proof.
- Block actual owned TLS handler; Quiesce cannot return/handoff while read in flight. Release/cancel actual read, confirm client connection closure before clean handoff. After completed or failed shutdown, every future read returns Closed before provider/metadata access. Existing queued shutdown regression remains intact.
- Clean handoff exact same read binding resumes; changed CA/endpoint/project/reader binding, nil↔enabled downgrade/upgrade, replaced registry/lock, changed cell/session or restored valid metadata prefix deny. Fresh bootstrap only: no fixture migration loophole to make this pass.

SEQUENCING / SOURCE BOUNDARIES:
Root review this design first. Then bounded implementation owns credentialstaging only plus finite runner/tests/docs/readonly CI extension when explicitly coordinated; leaves credentialobservation's accepted production code, manager/localmetadata/common journal/module unchanged unless a real composition failure is separately reported/reviewed. Source/root/localagent retain next heavy windows; author/read only now. Root .6.4 still awaits fresh default isolated acceptance, and .6.5 real guard composition stays open. Native TLS wire proof establishes protocol/closure with synthetic principals, not real Cloud/IAM/KMS/namespace permissions or workflow/worker readiness.

design:
READ-ONLY CANARY DESIGN (2026-10-30). No frozen18-file edits, credentials, authenticated calls, network probes, builds or cloud mutations. This is a proposed separate bounded slice, not a completed CredentialCanary integration.

DECISION: first contract should be observational-only temporal-candidate-namespace-auth-observation-v1. A fresh exact candidate key authenticates as its expected namespace-scoped SA/API-key, reads the exact Cloud namespace birth and a named data-plane namespace at independently configured TLS endpoints. It proves only that finite authenticated read during the recorded interval. It cannot authorize promotion, workflow execution/write, task-queue access, worker polling, worker readiness, mTLS, Nexus, SearchAttribute mutation or future credential validity. Existing retained actor remains staging-only and manager VerifyCandidates=false. Do not plug this into default manager: current verifyCandidate treats every probe error as canary failure/compensation (credential_manager.go:493-508), while retained mode must not revoke or change phase. First integration should be a separately reviewed actor-private ObserveStaged activity/method returning diagnostics only; no CredentialVerified, journal mutation, rotation or cleanup on result. A promotion-capable future contract must separately pin data-plane namespace UUID to Cloud birth and perform the actual required workflow/worker proof; it is not a rename of this observation.

PINNED PRIMARY SDK EVIDENCE:
- operator-v2/go.mod:7,11-15 pins Secrets Manager1.50.7, Temporal API1.63.5, Cloud SDK0.21.0, Go SDK1.50.0, gRPC1.83.2.

CreatedDate:111-114 is VERSION creation date, not SECRET birth. It returns no KMS ID. The Go SDK yields []byte binary without requiring Base64 decode (:119-131); reject SecretString/mixed output for this binary-only store.
- Cloud SDK api/cloudservice/v1/request_response.pb.go:72-82,133-145 has ServiceAccount principal oneof + optional PrincipalApiKey. identity/v1/message.pb.go:1354-1382 pins SA ID/spec/state/CreatedTime; :1564-1591 key ID/spec/state/CreatedTime; :1683-1710 immutable owner fields, display/marker/expiry/Disabled. - Cloud namespace/v1/message.pb.go:1629-1682 exposes qualified Namespace, CreatedTime, endpoints, state and ProjectId; it does NOT expose data-plane NamespaceInfo.Id.
- Temporal API workflowservice/v1/request_response.pb.go:342-350 DescribeNamespace accepts Namespace or Id; WeakConsistency=false is the default persistence/read-after-write mode. :406-409 returns NamespaceInfo; namespace/v1/message.pb.go:28-36 has Name/State/Id but no creation time. - Cloud SDK cloudclient/apikey_credentials.go:17-41 uses APIKeyReader, requires TLS unless explicitly insecure and materializes an authorization string; options.go:40-87 supports APIKeyReader, explicit HostPort/TLS/APIVersion and DisableRetry. Prefer narrow generated Cloud/Data APIs over worker/client startup, which can make extra startup RPCs.

READER CONSTRUCTION / AUTHORITY:
Create a new owned provider package with private opaque payload holders (private pointer, redacted all-format including %p/nested cases, JSON/text rejection, synchronous lifetime, close on every path). Public API Observe(ctx, SecretVersionRef) returns only typed safe Observation/error. Inputs are references, never KeyMaterial, token, SDK response, gRPC metadata, private key or arbitrary URL. Production constructor receives trusted immutable endpoint/TLS/project/namespace/owner/store/KMS bindings and explicit narrow AWS clients plus read-only CredentialJournal/OutcomeLedger loaders; it constructs candidate-only narrow gRPC connections inside the secure activity. Package-private fake transport constructors can test bytes/metadata using synthetic material; no public raw-token getter or generic permit factory.
A future actor-private read guard holds actual admission/session and full lifecycle mutex+registry lock, verifies exact staged slot/stage/attempt/write/key and immutable runtime reservations, and drains the complete read before shutdown/handoff. Do not reuse the current create CandidateGuard (it rightly permits StoreRequested only), export shared Gate, or relax retained phase whitelist. Recheck metadata versions after lock and after read; any missing/uncertain metadata/registry or changed admission/birth denies. An SDK timeout does not prove provider absence, though reads do not create mutation finality.
Before secret fetch, independently load exact Staged CredentialState and MetadataVerified Outcome for WriteID; require same owner, namespace birth/incarnation, store, slot/stage/attempt/candidate, SA/key immutable ID/birth/create receipts, encrypted candidate ref and VersionID=WriteID. Canonical ARN comes ONLY from the persisted successful exact CreateSecret receipt, never a name lookup/tag match. Require exact allowed AWS account/region, ARN/name coherence and receipt provenance. DescribeSecret(SecretId=that full ARN) independently verifies secret birth=Outcome.CreatedAt, KMS=exact fixture key, ownership/write tags, undeleted/unrotated state and expected version map, using the same finite checks as existing store.validMetadata (:341-365). GetSecretValue uses SecretId=exact full ARN, VersionId=exact WriteID, VersionStage absent. Verify returned ARN/name/VersionId exactly. Output CreatedDate is version birth: bound/validate it independently but NEVER compare it as if it were secret birth. Enforce nonempty bounded SecretBinary<=65536, SecretString nil; no Base64 decode in Go. Drop SDK ResultMetadata and all raw provider text, and keep copied bytes only within activity/provider memory.
IAM: separate explicitly configured reader principal gets GetSecretValue (and required DescribeSecret) only on exact candidate ARN plus Decrypt only on exact fixture KMS via Secrets Manager and exact secret encryption context. It has no secret create/Put/activation/delete/build/AssumeRole/PassRole rights. Exact VersionId is a request/data boundary, NOT an assumed IAM version-level restriction; do not invent secretsmanager:VersionId condition support. Existing sandbox candidate policy remains deny-all until separately reviewed exact stage2 update. A different IAM principal is not magically non-exfiltrating: the activity/code/TLS/log boundary remains trusted.

FINITE CALL PLAN / PROOF:
Within fresh bounded activity, retain no caches and use one immutable candidate version. Suggested deadline min(start+10s, key expiry minus small margin), bounded AWS attempts=1 and strict allowed-method/credential attempt budget for read-only gRPC. Limit to: DescribeSecret; GetSecretValue; Cloud GetCurrentIdentity; Cloud GetNamespace before data read; Data DescribeNamespace{Name=exact qualified namespace,WeakConsistency=false}; Cloud GetNamespace recheck. There are no namespace/user/key/workflow list calls or mutations. Re-read safe metadata/admission after operations, close both candidate-only connections and clear owned byte buffers before returning. TLS source endpoint and SNI must match trusted binding. Go authorization strings/SDK/TLS copies cannot be proven zeroized; claim no serialization/history/logging and bounded lifetime, not process compromise resistance or cryptographic erasure.
Identity proof: require ServiceAccount principal, exact expected SA ID/name/birth/marker, ACTIVE, namespace-scoped WRITE access to exact namespace and no account/project broad Access fields. Require nonnil PrincipalApiKey exact expected key ID/birth/owner=that SA/display+marker/expiry, enabled and ACTIVE. No absent PrincipalApiKey or user/admin principal fallback. Cloud GetNamespace must match exact account-qualified name/birth, ACTIVE/API-key enabled, and independently pinned ProjectId. Data result must match exact name and registered state. With no independently pinned data-plane UUID, its hashed ID is explicitly observational and cannot grant promotion; unknown/missing ID fails even observational proof rather than inventing identity.
Safe Observation DTO: schema1; exact finite Contract; trusted Owner; SlotID/StageID/AttemptID; NamespaceID and NamespaceIncarnationID; StoreID/CandidateID/WriteID/VersionID; SA/key IDs copied from independently pinned expected metadata only; CredentialJournalVersion and OutcomeLedgerVersion; EndpointBindingDigest; hashes of bounded observed key/SA/namespace native versions and observed data-plane ID; StartedAt/ObservedAt/ExpiresAt. Timestamp must fall inside actual fresh call and before key expiry; endpoint/proof contract are typed finite fields, not author input. Return success DTO only after all checks. No raw material/header/SDK body/provider message/raw opaque ResourceVersion. Fixed error codes distinguish secret read unknown, authorization/authentication rejected, identity evidence unsupported, binding/metadata changed, expired, canceled and deadline; raw err never wrapped/returned/logged. PermissionDenied/unsupported principal metadata is not proof of a bad candidate and must retain the stage.

COMPATIBILITY / PERMISSION GAPS:
Existing CanaryAttestation (credential_types.go:143-149) only has incarnation/key/version/Passed/time; no finite contract/SA/slot/stage/metadata/endpoint binding. Existing verifyCandidate validates only this weaker shape and writes CredentialVerified. Do not silently adapt observational proof into that bool. Adding a future finite attestation contract and deliberate manager/runtime compatibility is a separate reviewed change. Namespace-scoped SELF principal GetCurrentIdentity/GetNamespace/PrincipalApiKey population and data-plane read permission are still unproven in this account; pinned SDK structure proves fields exist, not that scoped Cloud grants work. No account-admin fallback or credential/bootstrap mutation. Namespace quota question remains open. Read-only observations do not prove write/worker authorization and do not establish future permission continuity.

NEGATIVE / FAULT TEST MATRIX (future implementation):
1. Missing/unknown/unbound ledger, non-Staged phase, foreign owner/birth/store/slot/stage/attempt/write/key/SA or stale versions -> zero GetSecretValue and zero gRPC auth.
2. Wrong ARN/name/account/region/resource birth/KMS/tags/deleted/rotated metadata -> deny. Different valid VERSION CreatedDate vs SECRET CreatedAt must not cause a false mismatch.

4. Every formatting verb including %p/nested containers, JSON/text, SDK errors, provider versions, result/error/status/captured activity payloads and durable frame scan use unique synthetic token sentinel and prove no disclosure; closed handles deny reuse. No real values.
5. Inherited admin authorization/routing context, ambient key reader/env, insecure/wrong-SNI/foreign endpoint/proxy or extra gRPC method -> deny or demonstrably scrub, and assert only exact candidate authorization reaches fake handler. No leaked connection retained beyond activity.
6. User/wrong SA/wrong key/wrong owner/birth/permissions/missing PrincipalApiKey/disabled/expired/nonACTIVE/unknown enum -> safe unsupported/mismatch diagnostic, no data-plane call.
7. Cloud birth/project/name changes before/after data read; wrong data-plane name/ID/state; separately pinned ID mismatch in future stronger contract -> deny.
8. Stale/future/expired cached attestations, metadata/admission/session change while waiting, cancel/deadline, late response or attempt-budget exceed -> no proof and stage retained; no DeleteApiKey/DeleteCandidate/journal phase transition or promotion.
9. Standalone default tests use injected owned synchronous fakes, no network/exec. Optional actual TLS fault proof only under owned opt-in isolated tier, then separately reviewed exact sandbox own allow/deny fixture proof after namespace/principal/IAM prerequisites. Never use production or absent-name stand-ins.

title: Observe canonical Service EndpointSlices independently from allocation and traffic proof
description: Typed Service allocation/spec observation deliberately reports BackendReadiness NotEvaluated. Add a separately reviewed read-only EndpointSlice capability pinned to the canonical owned Service UID, runtime namespace incarnation and current accepted workload intent. Service-name/managed-by labels alone are not authority; enumerate bounded slices with exact owner references and independently validate endpoint pod/workload identity rather than treating any selector match as trusted. Keep endpoint conditions, publication lag and actual network-path verification separate.
design:
Read-only design proposal, no code/source changes. EndpointRead carries original independently retained ServiceRead plus DeploymentRead, not public runtime DeploymentReceipt or supplied descendant UID/count lists. Observer freezes both bodies, freshly calls current exact Service and Deployment full-spec observers, and pins one namespace incarnation/owner/revision. Fetch discovery/v1 EndpointSlices using exact Service-name only as a discovery filter; no managed-by prefilter that could hide conflicting slices. Every relevant slice must independently show exact current Service controller UID/name, expected numeric TCP target-port set and single-stack family. managed-by and ownerRefs are consistency facts, not authenticated creator identity. A foreign/malformed relevant slice makes evidence incomplete rather than silently disappearing. Follow each endpoint targetRef to direct canonical Pod GET and ReplicaSet GET: exact namespace/name/UID, address belongs to current Pod family, matching Service membership, explicit Pod Ready and no deletion, current controller chain Pod->ReplicaSet->exact Deployment UID; compare RS selector/template relation rather than labels alone. Deployment observation verifies only top-level accepted spec and current status; it does not prove descendants.

Lists use finite page size/count/slices/endpoints/unique Pods/RS/response postdecode budget/total deadline, continuation RV consistency and repeated-token rejection. 410/partial/cap/conflicting duplicates returns incomplete; never healthy from a truncated subset. Identical duplicate endpoints deduplicate by Pod UID/family/address/portset; count distinct Pods rather than addresses. Recheck Namespace/Service/Deployment after sampling; any identity/spec/generation change invalidates sample. This is a bounded observed interval, not an atomic cross-resource snapshot/future fence; resource versions across kinds cannot be ordered or compared as one clock. Resource caps apply to the trusted pinned typed API contract, not proof against adversarial wire decoder allocation.

API effective nil defaults are Ready=true, Serving=true, Terminating=false; preserve explicit presence/defaulted count. Eligibility additionally requires fresh PodReady=True and no termination. Conflicting slice versus Pod conditions are Waiting/Unverified rather than optimistic eligibility. Empty publication is WaitingPublication, no failure of the Deployment implied. Existing Service baseline denies publishNotReadyAddresses. Opaque safe output: fixed code, Complete/Partial, distinct-Pod and ready/serving/terminating/unverified counts, independent start/completion timestamps, owning Service/Deployment metadata and sampled-version digests; no addresses, authored spec, raw condition messages or private refs.

Architectural choice pending root: current ownerRef ancestry cannot prove creation origin or unchanged Pod payload because Deployment and RS controllers adopt orphans. Prefer first slice explicitly current-ancestry endpoint-publication observation, not standalone promotion authority. Stronger complete Pod admission/defaulted body equivalence needs a separately reviewed explicit workload verifier capability; public DeploymentReceipt is insufficient. No generic mutation/EndpointSlice writes/DNS/packet/HTTP traffic readiness. Proposed tests cover nil condition semantics, duplicate conflict, foreign/missing owner hidden by manager filter, stale/replaced Pod/RS UID, copied labels, wrong IP/ports, partial paging/timeouts, parent/source change and safe output; actual owned fixture later creates real Deployment+Service with no-ready/ready publication and controlled wrong-owner slice.
acceptance_criteria: Explicit bounded pagination/duplicate aggregation and current serviceUID/namespaceUID/workload binding; defined nil/ready/serving/terminating semantics and stale/replaced/foreign/spoofed slice handling; no readiness from publishNotReadyAddresses. Actual owned local API proof covers delayed/no-ready endpoints, wrong owner and workload transition. Endpoint observations do not claim DNS resolution or packet delivery; those require independent probes.

description: Audit and port the embedded Python buildspec wrapper into maintained Go code. Preserve original image ENTRYPOINT/CMD argument behavior. design: Maintained package internal/lambdawrapper, cmd/registry-lambda-wrapper and new artifact/native harness scripts only. Scope is local runtime/compiler artifact evidence; no existing buildspec/source/provider or go.mod edits. Core snapshots execution-only env/argv behind opaque private-pointer handles with safe fmt/JSON, validates bounded duplicate/unknown/case-sensitive JSON and all projection grants before fetching, pins full standard-aws ARN+version plus property/env/file mapping against trusted installation/function/project/component/account/region policy. Policy construction is not ownership authentication. Existing TMPRL_ORIGINAL_* ABI preserves argv concatenation and native exec without shell expansion; PATH lookup uses explicit child environment. No injected secret enters synthesized argv. Bootstrap absent => secret reads off. Explicit trusted FD3 JSON may supply policy and explicit credentials; FD is not sealed and generic Lambda delivery is unproved. Lazy SDK client is HTTPS fixed-region host, normal TLS, no ambient credentials/config/proxies/redirects/retries/logging, finite timeout/header/body bounds, response duplicate checks before SDK decoding and exact response ARN/version. All provider errors collapse to fixed codes without retained raw causes. File manifest path is an allowlisted logical name, never followed; fresh 0700 tmp directory and 0600 exclusive files set only approved PathEnv variables. Primary error retains CleanupIncomplete flag; handoff is single-use and cleanup follows failed exec. title: Implement scoped service-account and API-key credential staging
description: Implement Temporal Cloud namespace-scoped service-account/API-key capability behind official SDK transport and explicit trusted namespace/incarnation bindings. design: Implemented credential staging in internal/providers/temporalcloud with official Cloud SDK types behind a separate narrow CredentialTransport. A safe linearizable journal slot per namespace incarnation records intent/attempt/expiry, step receipts and owned IDs before side effects; another attempt cannot bypass unresolved/verified stages. Pre-provisioned scoped SA bindings are supported; unknown SA create may replay only the exact async idempotent request, never broad account listing/adoption. API-key token stays in private KeyMaterial with redacted formatting, serialization rejection, synchronous encrypted-store use and invalidation afterward. No raw SDK response/exception is persisted. Candidate secret identity is separate per attempt; immutable VersionID must equal pre-generated 64-hex WriteID. Unknown store outcomes retain keys; final-not-committed requires a strong store guarantee excluding delayed commit, not absence. Lost one-time token recovery never invents a token: it verifies exact provider operation/input, scoped SA, durable unique attempt marker/spec/expiry and creation-time window, then requires a unique owner-filtered key match before compensation. Multiple/ambiguous matches stop without revocation. Canary resolves an immutable secret version entirely inside activity/store boundary and waits for key ACTIVE metadata. Canary failure is recorded separately from cleanup errors; only verified owned key/version is revoked, pending deletion is not completion, fulfilled delete plus absence is confirmed before atomic inactive candidate cleanup. Previously verified absence is idempotent. No activation, runtime secret overwrite, full rotation, mTLS protocol or concrete encrypted backend is claimed; follow-ups created under .9.

Stable NamespaceParent identity omits mutable resourceVersion/revision/epoch so ordinary parent edits do not rename application children. Local child Intent preserves logical names such as backend and derives idempotency from complete owner, scope and parent UID/provenance. Namespaced created records/observations bind the parent UID, independent canonical child UID, owner and creation provenance. AuthorizeCreate and BindCreated revalidate current parent proof; returned parent preconditions explicitly REQUIRE serialized/drained parent namespace lifecycle and expected UID annotation. A pre-read or ordinary read-only admission webhook cannot claim atomic create protection. Namespaced mutations revalidate parent proof, parent UID marker and record binding, then reuse common ownership policy for exact child UID/version/revision/writer checks. They require provider conditional mutation and return canonical child and parent preconditions. Generic Context still rejects local names and mismatched scope; child exceptions cannot authorize AWS/Temporal/cluster-scoped resources. title: Implement Go durable rollout coordinator and recovery contracts
description: Build a small Temporal Go entity workflow around one-action engine activity execution. Preserve typed desired/reconcile identity, latest pending signal, settled failure status and bounded polling; separate safe failure/cleanup/publication facts and retain queryable state. Use explicit worker/activity registration and injected engine factory; no production endpoints or credentials. Add SDK deterministic tests first and separately track real local-server Go replay proof.
design: New workflow type registry.project.v2 uses typed, level-triggered desired signals and one engine step per activity. Pending desired state is coalesced only between completed capability steps; duplicate/rejected signals do not reset timers or accelerate provider polling. Durable attempt epochs separate intentionally revisited intents from retries/Continue-As-New, so runtime namespace names are never operator-reused after an observed UID. Carry contains pending/current/last started intent, attempt counters, last settled identity and safe projections. Cleanup runs through a distinct injected activity; finalization remains blocked on failure and retries only when signaled, while cancellation uses a disconnected cleanup call and safe terminal status in cancellation details. Provider errors cross engine.SafeBoundaryError before Temporal conversion; terminal rollout failure is a native non-retryable activity error carrying bounded projection details, leaving the actor available for a later intent. SDK deterministic tests are being added; real Go server replay and durable backend integration remain separate proof.
acceptance_criteria: SDK tests cover success/failure, bounded retries, new reconcile after failure, duplicate/stale signals, cancellation/cleanup intent and state handoff; activity errors contain only safe diagnostics; code performs no provider I/O in workflow handlers.
notes: Implemented activity-safe failure boundary (pointer result avoids serializing invalid zero projections), native terminal-rollout activity failures, verified returned identities, retry-state diagnostics from actual ActivityError, durable attempt epochs, coalesced signal/poll timers, cleanup/finalization retry and cancellation outcome details. SDK tests now include success, later intent after failure, duplicate/stale/foreign signals, revisited-source epochs, bounded retry/no secret leakage, pending signal Continue-As-New, cancellation with complete or pending cleanup, initial finalization and blocked-state polling. Real local Go history/replay proof still needs its own integration tier.

Real Go server history proof is separate.

title: Implement scoped Go Temporal Cloud namespace adapter and contract tests
description: Use official current Cloud API protobuf/client SDK behind an injected transport. design: Implemented scoped official Cloud SDK adapter under internal/providers/temporalcloud. SDK cloud-sdk v0.21.0 is confined here and explicit supported API version is v0.24.0. Narrow transport exposes only exact namespace CRUD, namespace tags and async-operation reads. Constructor requires explicit allowed binding/creation intents and authority; no account listing/global management exists. TLS connection requires explicit endpoint/API version/credentials, rejects insecure TLS, clones caller config and disables nested SDK retries. Per-RPC deadlines and typed error classification support bounded orchestration retries externally. Trusted fixture bindings pin namespace name.account AND CreatedTime in canonical incarnation ID because names are reusable. Every write requires externally serialized/drained writer guard, owner/epoch/lease checks, current independent namespace birth observation and expected resourceVersion; update/delete transmit that version to provider. Tag API lacks version CAS, so a separate global capability and external serialization are explicit. Namespace patch clones provider spec and preserves unknown fields, supports retention/fairness/protection/description/search-attribute additions and rejects unsupported removal/type changes. Creation requires pre-persisted owner intent/fingerprint, fixed approved project/region/budget, delete protection and deterministic async UUID; no name-only create-or-adopt path. Recovery verifies exact operation receipt and echoed create payload plus birth window before minting a binding; absent or unsupported evidence fails closed. Failed transport responses preserve recovery IDs, while raw SDK/async/guard messages are not retained in typed diagnostic errors. Namespace deletion is separate from protection disablement, returns pending after request, and recognizes verified absence idempotently. No provider calls/authenticated Cloud access occurred.
acceptance_criteria: Fake transport tests validate exact request IDs/resource versions, unknown-create recovery, ownership conflicts, typed auth/transient errors and no mutation after invalid scope; actual SDK transport builds with explicit credentials/endpoints and no default production authority.
notes:

title: Add verified loopback-only Temporal history and recovery test tier

Tests cannot supply endpoint/auth/other unaudited options or spawn downloads/processes. Verify the PID is the sole listener on that port before client launch, monitor server lifetime, and stop only owned process groups in finally. Reuse the baseline credential/home/file restrictions. Test-time Python audit-visible network/process attempts persist and fail even if caught; native transport is constrained by OS rules. SBPL's localhost filter includes IPv4/IPv6 at the chosen port; actual plugin target is numeric 127.0.0.1. Separate hash-locked acquisition from sandboxed execution; no production dependency changes.
acceptance_criteria: Repeatable local command runs representative history/recovery cases without AWS/Kube/Temporal Cloud access; network policy and native Temporal core transport behavior are negatively tested; selected/skipped tests and missing prerequisites are explicit.
notes: Implemented scripts/run_operator_temporal_tests.py, scripts/tests/test_operator_temporal_recovery.py, scripts/requirements-operator-tests.in and hash-locked .lock. Remaining limits: macOS-only OS sandbox; trusted CLI has broader loopback access for its internals; native denied attempts may not enter Python audit log; time-skipping/other history suites/Kubernetes/cloud integrations remain excluded. Official testing guidance checked at https://docs.temporal.io/develop/python/best-practices/testing-suite .

description: Produce reviewable sandbox-only AWS and Temporal fixture plans in separate state/source paths. Evidence writes only the dedicated AES256 S3 object prefix. State uses a distinct versioned-bucket proposal and native lockfile example, unreachable by operator/build/runtime/controller policies. Cloud Lambda, external-secret controller and invoker are inactive; a separate inactive exact-function/PassRole extension documents the additional review and boundary changes needed. Temporal baseline uses separate principals and pre-provisioned exact namespaces; account namespace creation, global readers, Nexus and unscoped service-account management are disabled. Primary docs support current action/resource/condition shapes, including CodeBuild status/stop on project resources; JSON review matrix records remaining proof per capability. Shared-account quotas and timeout/source/compute overrides need a fixture broker/real headroom proof; defaults alone are not an enforcement guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed action/resource matrix and policy validation fixtures include transitive/reciprocal paths; no production source/build role/bootstrap secret or global readers access; unresolved effective-policy assumptions listed.
notes: Root reviewed and accepted the inert design artifacts. Final hardening requires secretsmanager:KmsKeyArn on CreateSecret separately from dependent TagResource authorization; tests reject foreign/default keys. Latest go test -race ./testinfra -count=1 and go vet ./testinfra passed after that change. Primary action/resource/condition matrix is stored in action-resource-review.json. No cloud calls, source deployment or actual permission proof; all real trust/KMS/namespace bindings and effective-policy verification remain pending in .3.3.

title: Implement sandbox ownership and identity rules with offline negative tests
description: Encode trusted environment/installation/project UID context, separate disposable run names from stable production identity, derive disjoint roots and bounded names, reject unowned/adopt-by-name/raw-ID mutations and cross-environment secret/Nexus/role aliases. Carry stable intent/idempotency provenance through recovery and owner/writer distinctions. No provider calls or production configuration changes.
design: Implemented a standard-library-only ownership package under operator-v2/internal/ownership. Validated immutable Context copies explicit provider scopes and stable environment/installation/project UID ownership; disposable lifetime alone adds a run ID. Root derivation rejects the legacy production prefix and ancestor roots, preserves a full 128-bit digest under truncation, includes provider/purpose/scope in names and leaves operation IDs out of stable resource names. Intent/PathIntent generate stable operation idempotency provenance; AuthorizeCreate validates the writer before an adapter create; BindCreated supports unknown-outcome recovery only with independent provider owner, revision, fingerprint, epoch and creation-token evidence. Records and observations require canonical provider IDs and exact authority. AWS supported named ARN shapes additionally require ID/name coherence; opaque KMS key/Route53 IDs fail closed pending reviewed adapters. Authorize handles update/adoption/promotion/cleanup with exact ledger/observation ID, scope, owner, provenance, expected revision, fingerprint and writer epoch/expiry. It returns action-bound provider preconditions, never a lock. Conditional mode requires a provider version. Unsupported fencing requires a conspicuous externally serialized/drained assertion, preserved in output; this package does not establish that guarantee. Provider observations, writer coordinator/clock, durable ledger and enforcement of returned preconditions remain adapter responsibilities. Legacy resource import requires a separate reviewed path, not weakening sandbox root validation.
acceptance_criteria: Offline tests demonstrate separation after truncation, same-name project cases, explicit context validation, stale cleanup/name reuse, foreign-ID rejection and retry ownership recovery.
notes: Validation: go test ./internal/ownership -count=1 passed; go test -race ./internal/ownership -count=1 passed after final changes; go vet ./internal/ownership passed. Offline negative cases cover configuration, scope-copy mutation, full-identity truncation, purpose/provider differentiation, stable vs disposable identities, path traversal, creation recovery, name-only adoption, foreign owners/IDs/accounts/regions/partitions, same-account prod ARN laundering, missing provenance, stale revisions/cleanup/epochs, expired writer lease and missing provider fencing. No cloud calls or production files. Parent peer review identified ARN/name coherence, implemented and tested. Reviewed rollout planner separately and reported route UID/version race and failure-outcome persistence ordering; root accepted both findings.
close_reason: Ownership library and offline acceptance tests implemented and validated; provider enforcement and real cloud proof remain explicitly separate tasks.

title: Design and prove isolation for tests in shared cloud accounts
description: Map every shared identity before any real cloud execution. Cluster/color scopes task queues and entity workflow IDs, but derive.py hardcodes project-based Temporal namespace, ECR, secret and DNS identities; serverless_names.py hardcodes Lambda/IAM identities; namespace reader workflows are account-wide. Design an explicit environment and run ownership context threaded through create, observe, update and delete operations. Use a distinct operator Temporal namespace and test target namespaces, dedicated AWS test identity with API-specific ARN and tag restrictions, tightly scoped PassRole/build service roles/secrets/artifacts, isolated local Kubernetes context, separate DNS, and owned cleanup records. Keep production bootstrap/admin credentials out of the test process. Verify current Temporal Cloud permissions and availability of any project/custom-role features rather than assuming them. Bound concurrency/creation budgets for shared quotas. Keep any stateful test infrastructure in separate state and no production GitOps source path.
design:
READ-ONLY ISOLATION ASSESSMENT (2026-10-29)

Decision and scope
Use local Kubernetes and Temporal for the first replacement slice. Real-cloud work is a separate opt-in lane with a pre-provisioned sandbox identity, explicit ownership context, disjoint names, and action-specific permissions. This review establishes architecture and test requirements; it does not prove the effective policies of the real account. No authenticated cloud calls, credentials/state inspection, production edits, or deployments were performed. Task stays in progress until implementation and independent authorization evidence exist.

Repository evidence
1. derive.py:16-20 fixes namespace/ECR/secret/domain roots. derive.py:81-99 colors project/course workflow IDs and :142-149 colors task queues, but :130-139 deliberately leaves reader sync and grants account-wide. Crashable workspace seed at :152-160 has user/project but no environment.
2. kube.py:69-93 lists all cluster-scoped DemoProject/InstruqtCourse objects without selection; watch.py:177-211 reconciles each. Labels alone will not hide tests from the existing production watcher. Keep test CRs in a disposable local cluster. A future shared-cluster design requires both writers to enforce ownership selection; editing only the new watcher cannot protect against the old one.
3. watch.py:171-174 and :228-248 starts the shared namespace-reader sync on activation. Disable and exclude that capability in sandbox code/credentials. Separate queues do not isolate the global group or workflow identity.
4. infra/irsa.tf:218-226 explicitly describes shared blue/green external authority; :243-273 grants ECR/secret changes and deletion across the production root; :279-288 permits starting the production shared build project; :321-379 grants Lambda and IAM role mutation and PassRole across the production prefix.
5. TRANSITIVE AUTHORITY: infra/codebuild.tf:39-73 gives the build service role production ECR writes and project/platform secret reads, :99-109 adds public ECR pushes, :115-136 accepts operator buildspec overrides under that role in a privileged container. A narrow test operator that can StartBuild on this project inherits an execution path into this authority. Never share this project/service role for tests.
6. resources.py:545-558 deliberately lets onboarding previews read another project's secrets via secrets-from. resources.py:5641 maps shared secrets to platform/shared. Disallow these aliases in the sandbox unless an exact immutable test-only capability explicitly grants them. Also disallow arbitrary awsIamRoleArn, remote secret paths, CodeBuild project names, target namespace IDs, and Nexus caller references that bypass derived ownership.
7. clusters/blue/addons/external-secrets/stores/clustersecretstore.yaml names platform-secrets and uses AWS Secrets Manager with controller identity. A test ExternalSecret referencing it can gain authority through the controller, even with a narrow operator principal. Use a local fake secret adapter initially, then a distinct namespaced store and test-only controller identity; do not install the production ClusterSecretStore locally.
8. activities/temporal_cloud.py:582-608 finds and updates Nexus endpoints by declared name; :640-648 says names are account-wide. The initial sandbox must reject arbitrary endpoint names and production caller/target IDs, or keep Nexus cloud operations disabled pending scoped permissions.
9. activities/temporal_cloud.py:2117-2179 has raw-ID/name deletion helpers. :2463-2492 obtains API-key and service-account IDs from secret content, :2511-2546 resolves a namespace then disables protection/deletes it. A valid-looking foreign ID or secret reference must never authorize cleanup; ownership needs independent verification at the adapter boundary. Existing finalizer/retain policy is useful but does not itself enforce an environment authorization boundary.
10. infra/rollout_diagnostics.tf:1-5 shares a bucket across colors; :106+ permits writes across clusters/*. A separate prefix under this same bucket is not independently isolated by today's writer policy. Use a distinct test artifact store or explicit narrow policies with enforced ownership.
11. projects/operator/registry.yaml builds this repository's registry/worker/Dockerfile and renders the self-managed operator; do not put the prototype in the current worker build/context or production GitOps input directories. Keep source changes local and additive until reviewed.

Ownership model
Define an immutable EnvironmentContext configured by the process, not accepted from a project spec: environment ID, run ID, trusted account/region/cluster identity, operator Temporal namespace, resource root, DNS zone/domain allowlist, capability set, quota budget, lease expiry, and owner identity. Each reconciliation also carries project UID (not only name), generation/revision, and an operation ID. ResourceRef records provider type, canonical immutable ID/ARN/UID, owner environment/run/project UID, creation operation, and spec fingerprint. A durable run resource ledger records intent BEFORE creation and ID after creation; retries recover using provider idempotency and verified ownership.

Default root must be disjoint from existing production roots, e.g. registry-lab-<environment>-<run> for dashed names and registry-lab/<environment>/<run> for paths. Do not place tests beneath tmprl-dem-cld/tests: the current production IAM wildcard still covers it. Include the full identity seed when hash-truncating names; changing environment or run must change every namespace/function/role/secret/repo/endpoint/workflow identity. No implicit adoption by name: existing resources require matching independent owner record and provider metadata/UID, otherwise fail closed. Verify before update, role passing, credential promotion, protection changes, deletion, or compensation. Missing/mismatched ownership or a changed provider ID is an actionable terminal isolation error. A lease prevents new mutations after expiry; cleanup is a separately scoped capability with a bounded grace period, not a blind prefix sweep. Ownership metadata is not trusted if supplied only by the resource request being tested.

Action/resource permission matrix (requirements, not installed policy)
- Local runner: no AWS/Cloud credentials, no production kubeconfig, no production Docker socket credentials or mounted cloud configuration; explicit local endpoints and cluster identity. Fake provider capabilities by default.
- Kubernetes watcher and runtime: disposable local API server and only that local cluster. Test CRs, RBAC, finalizers, status/catalog ConfigMaps, source resources and workload namespaces stay local. Cloud credentials never inherit a broad External Secrets or IRSA identity. Do not assume namespace RBAC limits cluster-scoped CR discovery.
- Temporal data plane: a dedicated operator test namespace, with credentials limited to it, distinct task queue/workflow prefixes, and separate test target namespaces/keys. No production histories, signals, schedules, worker-version updates, or queries requiring production access.
- Temporal namespace provisioning/control plane: baseline first uses pre-provisioned test namespaces and a narrowly scoped principal. Namespace creation is an account/project operation, not an existing-namespace permission. If testing creation is essential, use a bounded privileged fixture/provisioning path that returns approved IDs and never gives the operator production bootstrap credentials. Developer/project/custom-role availability and effective permissions must be verified in this account before relying on them. Namespace-scoped service accounts can be managed by Namespace Admins per official current docs; the current implementation's account-level SA creation path may require adaptation.
- Temporal service accounts/API keys/mTLS: mutate only exact approved test namespace-scoped identities and keys whose owner is verified. Never manage unscoped production service accounts; secrets cannot nominate foreign key IDs for deletion.
- Temporal reader groups/users: no capability in the first cloud test principal. Shared production group updates and user grants are prohibited. Test equivalent business logic with stubs; a later dedicated test group requires a separately reviewed account-level fixture.
- Temporal Nexus: initially stubbed/disabled. Later only explicit approved test project/endpoints, namespace targets and caller allowlists, with no production caller/target capability. Current docs include project-scoped and custom roles; availability and actual account permission behavior remain unverified.
- ECR private/public: allow required CRUD/push/read only on disjoint test repository ARNs in configured account and region. Global authorization-token actions may require Resource *, but confer no repository CRUD by themselves. Validate every action in the AWS service authorization table; constrain create request tags and update resource tags where supported. No production repository policy change or image/tag overwrite.
- Secrets Manager/KMS: exact test root and explicit test KMS key only, including candidate and rotation secrets. No production bootstrap/GitHub/DockerHub/shared-auth credentials; use separately provisioned test source/build secrets. No broad ListSecrets discovery unless a justified filtered read requirement exists. Enforce immutable ownership tag keys after create where supported; resource-name scope remains necessary.
- CodeBuild: a dedicated test project AND service role; StartBuild/BatchGet/Stop only this project, short timeout/concurrency. Test role ECR, secret, log, artifact and KMS authority is equally narrow. Restrict overrides and especially serviceRoleOverride; inspect each override permission and downstream service role. Do not reuse production codebuild:StartBuild access even if direct operator ECR/Secrets denies look safe.
- IAM/Lambda: initially cloud Lambda disabled until sandbox policies are proven. Later exact test role/function prefixes and immutable IDs; narrow CreateRole with an approved test permissions boundary; allow role policy/trust mutation only for test roles; exact iam:PassRole ARNs plus iam:PassedToService. No AssumeRole path into production roles, no wildcard policy attachment or boundary removal. Runtime Lambda roles, the Temporal invoke role and their trust/external IDs must share the same owner context. No production event source or Function URL setup.
- External Secrets/controller authority: only a dedicated test store and downstream identity, no production platform-secrets use. Trace role assumption and KMS permissions; validation must include what a controller can do on behalf of a test object.
- S3/logs/artifacts: distinct test bucket or exact scoped test root under demonstrably restricted policies, no production bucket/object overwrites or reads. Narrow logs groups and KMS keys. No ACL/policy mutation. Redact output and prevent diagnostic bundles from exposing keys.
- DNS/ingress: localhost or local test DNS first; later a delegated test-only zone and test certificate setup. No live swing record, wildcard routing, production hosted zone mutation, OAuth callback mutation, or shared TLS secret reuse.
- Instruqt/GitHub/other external publishers: no production token/push capability in the initial lane; fake publishing by default. Arbitrary repository build scripts run only with test service authority. Private source fixtures use independent read-only test access.

Transitive and reciprocal closure
Review effective permissions for operator -> StartBuild -> build role, operator -> PassRole -> Lambda execution role, operator/CR -> ExternalSecret -> controller role -> secret/KMS, Temporal principal -> service-account/API-key role, IAM AssumeRole/trust -> other roles, image build -> ECR tag -> deployed runtime, and credentials in artifact/log output. An action-level deny on the originating role does not constrain an independently privileged service role. Also review production -> test paths: current production role's prefix grants, resource policies/trust, tag discovery, shared group sync, GitOps delivery and watcher listing. Disjoint prefixes/local CRs reduce exposure without editing production, but real effective policies are not known here. Single active owner/fencing is required for any later production handoff.

Negative and failure tests
Offline: identity derivation for two environments/runs including truncation; same project names cannot share names/keys; project spec cannot override trusted context; reject foreign ARNs/IDs, wrong account/region/cluster, missing owner, retag attempts, secrets-from alias, Nexus prod targets, production CodeBuild project and role overrides; stale run cleanup cannot delete current run; name reuse with changed UID fails; retries recover from partial create; timeout/cancel cleanup touches only ledger-owned resources; missing owner fails before any provider mutation.
Policy review/simulation: validate each action/resource/condition combination, negative matching against synthetic production ARNs, plus transitive-role closure and tag create/update coverage. A simulator is supporting evidence only and cannot prove all resource/trust policies.
Later controlled account proof: no actual destructive calls against production. Use non-destructive policy/effective-permission evidence and dedicated sentinel fixtures created under reviewed production-equivalent deny rules. Test denied mutations against those sentinels, allowed test operations and cleanup, with provider request/audit references. Fail the lane if an expected deny succeeds. Prove real namespace/endpoint/SA permissions with dedicated fixtures, and verify runtime credential grants contain only test IDs. Root must review the fixture plan before cloud execution; this assessment creates no approval requirement beyond the stated production constraint.

Budget and stop policy
Proposed first cloud lane, contingent on actual spare account capacity: one active run, one target namespace at a time, one build at a time, bounded test secret/repository counts, 30-minute test deadline, bounded backoff/requests, and cleanup verification before another run. Do not reserve Lambda account concurrency or enable event sources until reviewed: reservations themselves can reduce production headroom. Increase capacities only from measured needs and spare quotas. Stop new mutations on first unexplained authorization success, owner mismatch, repeated throttling, deadline overrun, or unverified cleanup. Cleanup remains scoped and preserves original error/evidence. Shared accounts still share quotas/billing/control planes; no design can claim literally zero possible account impact from real account testing.

Official primary references checked
AWS StartBuild API: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/APIReference/API_StartBuild.html (buildspecOverride changes executable commands; serviceRoleOverride changes role).
AWS CodeBuild condition keys: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/action-context-keys.html (buildspec condition currently tests presence via Null, not buildspec contents).
AWS PassRole: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_passrole.html (scope role ARN and service; ResourceTag is not a reliable PassRole control).
AWS tag authorization: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_tags.html (action/service support varies).
Temporal permissions: https://docs.temporal.io/cloud/manage-access/permissions-reference and upstream https://github.com/temporalio/documentation/blob/main/docs/cloud/manage-access/permissions-reference.mdx (account, project, namespace scopes; Namespace Admin for scoped SA management).
Temporal custom roles: https://docs.temporal.io/cloud/manage-access/custom-roles (pre-release; resource IDs must already exist; do not depend on availability without account verification).


Architecture review addendum
Reviewed epic 2f4 design. Stable environment/installation/project identity is separate from ephemeral test-run identity. Run-derived resource names in this assessment apply to disposable test resources only; production namespaces, secret identities and service accounts must not change on every reconcile, process restart, or ordinary deployment. Operation/reconcile/run IDs are diagnostic/idempotency correlation, not authority to claim an existing resource.

Invariants for implementation:
- Resource ownership (stable) and active-writer lease/epoch (temporary) are distinct.
- Persist intent and stable idempotency token before create; add canonical provider ID after response or verified recovery. An unknown create outcome must not trigger a blind new identity.
- Every promote, rollback, destructive update and delete is conditional on expected owner/project UID, candidate revision, provider identity/version and active writer epoch.
- Where providers expose optimistic resource versions or conditional updates, adapters use them. An ownership check followed by an unconditional mutation has a time-of-check race; merely adding a lock/token to local state does not guarantee stale actors cannot write to an API that does not enforce it. Unsupported cases require serialized execution, draining and a conservative explicit handoff.
- Cleanup is monotonic and resumeable: requested deletion is not confirmed deletion. Remove the finalizer only after confirmed cleanup or explicit retain semantics with recorded retained IDs.
- A recreated resource with the same name and different UID/ID is a new object and never inherits cleanup authorization.
acceptance_criteria: Reviewed action/resource permission matrix; negative authorization tests and ownership tests show test principals cannot modify production resources, assuming production identities do not grant reciprocal access; cleanup rejects unowned resources; cloud quota budget, stop criteria and privilege-limited provisioning procedure are defined. No account changes as part of design alone.
notes: First read-only architecture pass complete. Sent key CodeBuild transitive-authority and reciprocal-isolation findings to /root. Implementation, effective-policy evidence, negative authorization proof and account feature verification remain pending; do not close parent. No source/config changes or cloud calls.
