title: Trace failure visibility and define a consistent diagnostic contract
description: Trace representative build, provider, rollout, credential, and teardown failures from activity through workflow status, CR status, catalog ConfigMaps, API, and UI. Existing code already stores activity failures, compensation outcomes and S3 rollout evidence; find where information is lost, stale, or hard to access. Define a common operation record with project/environment/reconcile identity, failed step, cause category, attempt/retry state, timestamps, workflow/run/activity event references, provider request IDs when available, resource and evidence links, cleanup outcome, and evidence-based next action. Redact secrets and make status publication failures visible. Preserve current user-facing contracts while planning additive changes.
design:
Design review, 2026-10-29. This is a proposed contract for review, not a deployed schema. Scope is repository evidence and design; no cloud calls or source/configuration edits.

Product outcome
For any project/reconcile or finalization, the catalog must answer: what failed, why we believe it failed, what the operator is doing now, whether serving production was affected, which cleanup remains, and what the person can safely do next. Unknown causes and stale observations must be explicit. Deep links and a copyable redacted diagnostic bundle should let teammates investigate the same operation without reconstructing it in a new agent session.

Current evidence and gaps
1. Builds: activities/builds/codebuild/execution.py:229-255 records terminal build status; :349-379 preserves build ID, resolved source, timestamps and CloudWatch deepLink. errors.py:106-125 turns terminal statuses into activity errors with status details, then recovers activityFailure. resources.py:4306-4318 intentionally gives catalog a bounded build summary and retains codebuild/lastError, but not the recovered activityFailure reference. Build provider evidence exists; a compact failure/event reference is missing from its projection.
2. Provider/credential: errors.py:73-100 and :154-178 classify typed gRPC/AWS auth/config/transient errors. workflows/demo_project.py:1623-1637 executes namespace creation with bounded retry; activities/external_resources/temporal.py:505-535 stages credentials; :601-626 converts runtime credential canary errors. workflows/demo_project.py:2242-2273 records rolloutFailure and compensationStatus after generic reconcile failure. resources.py:4291-4303 intentionally reduces external resources to phase/message/checkedAt via phase_summary at :4369-4376; catalog_status_entry at :4234-4276 does not expose rolloutFailure or compensationStatus. Preserve bounded summaries but add causality and drill-down references. Credential values must never be included.
3. Non-fatal warnings: workflows/demo_project.py:1639-1671 (DNS), :1673-1708 (tags), :1710-1739 (reader access) log and continue deliberately to avoid compensating healthy resources. This is correct recovery policy, but user status has no common warning projection. Warn on unresolved DNS/access metadata without falsely marking the whole deployment failed.
4. Rollout: workflows/demo_project_kubernetes_runtime.py:122-144, :198-241 creates stage-specific status for worker rollout/readiness/smoke failures. :470-550 separately captures diagnostics, route restoration, worker rollback, and candidate pruning. Diagnostics capture failure retains the candidate to preserve evidence. resources.py:4267-4271 DOES forward diagnostics (including prior failure fallback), but omits rollbackStatus, workerDeploymentRollbackStatus, rolloutFailure and compensationStatus. Original failure and recovery outcomes must remain distinct.
5. Evidence bounds: kube.py:1397-1414 explicitly limits pods/events/logs, avoids pod Secret/env serialization, and acknowledges logs can contain sensitive application output; :1451-1488 captures raw bounded log text. activities/rollout_diagnostics.py:130-192 uploads encrypted private S3 evidence with digest/partial metadata. No claim that existing log text is sanitized. Need safe summary redaction before publication and authorized evidence access; never copy raw logs into public catalog status.
6. Publication: activities/reconcile.py:1800-1843 main status activities call patch_status/patch_catalog_status with raise_errors=True. Thus the main workflow does NOT silently swallow publication failure; helper defaults at :1874-1950 are best-effort but not the main path. workflows/demo_project.py:2636-2656 writes CR first then catalog through separate strict activities. Partial publication is possible. Preserve operation cause when publication fails, and expose sink health separately rather than replacing root failure with a status-write error.
7. Freshness: activities/reconcile.py:1813,1836 adds reconcileKey to CR/status payload. resources.py:4234-4276 projection discards it and sets updatedAt to current projection time (:4243). server.py:232-248 loads JSON without a freshness comparison; :251-275 attaches status. A recent projection timestamp alone cannot establish that the desired generation/source was reconciled.
8. UI: server.py:251-275 preserves the projected status in the enriched /api/catalog response, but static/app.js:229-263 normalizeDemo drops project.status entirely; :290-298 maps all ordinary demos through that function. This is a direct visibility gap, not merely overly terse backend summaries. Ordinary project cards lack the lifecycle diagnostic data already carried by the API.
8a. API route disconnect and audience: static/app.js:292 fetches /api/registry. server.py:1274-1275 serves static load_registry for /api/registry; only /api/catalog at :1276-1277 calls catalog_payload and attaches live status. Thus ordinary UI never requests the enriched payload, then would also discard status in normalization. These are two separate broken boundaries. The enriched /api/catalog handler does not call authenticated_email. This proves only absence of a handler-level identity check; actual exposure also depends on ingress/platform auth and was not verified here. Richer internal diagnostics need an explicitly authorized endpoint/audience, while ordinary discovery can carry a safe bounded state.
9. Closed executions: server.py:1145-1174 queries a failed workspace for retained failure/compensation but falls back to "Environment provisioning failed. Try again." if no worker can answer. Terminal evidence must remain readable after workers retire.
10. Teardown: workflows/demo_project.py:797-799 calls _run_finalize outside the reconcile saga catch; :2344-2370 only publishes Finalized after deletion stages succeed. A failing teardown can therefore leave the previous projection, with the Temporal activity/history as the useful diagnostic. It needs explicit Finalizing/Blocked cleanup progress and failed resource references. Retain existing finalizer/ownership safety.
11. Causality: errors.failure_details at errors.py:128-147 walks the cause chain but flattens it into one dict, overwriting fields along the way. Record a bounded causal chain, stable root diagnostic and correlated child/activity references instead of assuming the final flattened activity identifies every relevant execution.

Proposed version 1 operation contract
DiagnosticOperation {schemaVersion:1, operationId, subject:{kind,name,uid,environment,runOwner}, intent:{action,reconcileKey,observedGeneration,sourceRevision}, workflow:{namespace,id,runId,workerBuildId}, sequence, state, currentStep, startedAt, progressedAt, completedAt, availability:{activeRevision,candidateRevision,routeState,confirmedAt}, primaryFailure?, warnings:[], recovery:{state,steps:[]}, evidence:[], nextActions:[]}.
State is Pending/Running/Waiting/Retrying/Succeeded/Failed/Cancelled/Finalizing/Finalized; availability is independent, and is Unknown unless observed. currentStep includes stable code, safe description, resource refs, last observed attempt, attempt limit if known, retry status (scheduled/exhausted/nonRetryable/unknown), lastAttemptAt and nextAttemptAt ONLY if authoritative. Do not imply a retry is scheduled from a generic retryable classification.
primaryFailure {diagnosticId,code,category,message,occurredAt,failedStep,causeChain:[{type,safeMessage}],activity:{type,id,scheduledEventId},childWorkflow?,provider:{service,errorCode,requestId},resources:[],evidenceIds:[]}. Categories include validation/config/auth/transient/build/readiness/smoke/cleanup/statusPublication/unknown. Stable codes drive remediation; code/provider evidence, not guessed strings, determines a next action.
recovery records each compensation/rollback/prune with independent outcome/error, retained resources and manual intervention indicator. Never overwrite primaryFailure with cleanup, evidence upload or status publication failure. For failed first-provision cleanup, show both failures.
Projection envelope {operation:boundedSummary,publication:{sourceSequence,projectedAt,sinks:[{name,state,lastSuccessAt,lastErrorCode}]},freshness:{desiredReconcileKey,observedReconcileKey,desiredGeneration,observedGeneration,lastProgressAt,state}}. Consumers compute Current/Reconciling/Stale/Unavailable honestly; age thresholds are configurable per operation type and are not equivalent to task liveness.
All status, structured logs and optional traces use operationId/diagnosticId/environment/subject UID/workflow IDs. Metrics use bounded labels (step/code/category/environment), not project/workflow/operation IDs or email. Unknown schema major versions render a safe unavailable message with an operation identifier; additional fields are backward-compatible.

Storage and availability
Use Temporal history as execution truth and existing private evidence storage for bulk material. First implementation requires no new service or database. Carry a compact operation summary and primary failure identity across Continue-As-New. Persist a terminal compact projection independently of workflow queries before workers retire; bounded retention/tombstones must cover teardown and expired evidence. A UI read must not depend on a matching historical worker remaining available.
Keep catalog projection intentionally bounded: proposed 8 KiB current summary per subject, 1 KiB safe message, cause chain <=8 entries, <=10 resource/evidence references, <=5 warnings and <=5 next actions. Signal truncation and provide evidence references. Enforce aggregate ConfigMap budget before writes and partition summaries by project if required; never put growing operation history or pod logs in the shared ConfigMap. Preserve last relevant failure reference after later success, labeled historical rather than current. Existing snapshot collection limits remain independently enforced. Expired/missing artifacts show explicit EvidenceExpired/Unavailable without destroying the root diagnostic. Reuse authenticated catalog access to resolve permitted evidence by opaque ID; do not expose bucket credentials or unrestricted S3 proxies.

Redaction and authorization
Project diagnostics may contain internal names; expose them only under the intended audience policy, which differs from public demo discovery. Build a safe allowlisted summary at the producer boundary, apply a shared recursive redaction policy to messages/URLs/known credential forms, and test again at API/bundle serialization. Never persist credentials, tokens, private keys, env values, auth headers or signed URL query parameters. Secret paths/resource IDs are references and may still require authorization. Private raw logs remain restricted and cannot be promised fully sanitized by regex. Do not blindly publish arbitrary provider exception strings. Evidence-download and diagnostic-bundle endpoints verify subject/environment ownership and the current viewer's authorization.

Example failure view (synthetic acceptance scenario, not an observed incident)
"Banking demo: candidate git-abc123 did not become ready. Kubernetes reports ImagePullBackOff; image pull returned unauthorized. The previous version git-def456 remains active (confirmed 14:32 UTC). Automatic rollout retry is exhausted after 3 observed attempts. Route restoration completed. Candidate resources were retained because evidence upload failed. Next: verify the candidate image and pull-role access; then request a reconcile. Do not delete the retained candidate until evidence is captured. [Workflow activity] [Pod events] [Build logs] [Cleanup details] [Copy redacted diagnostic]. Operation op-...; observed generation 12; desired generation 12; last progress 14:32 UTC." If route confirmation or exact cause is absent, say Unknown rather than asserting it.

Required contract tests
A. A representative CodeBuild failure retains safe provider error/build log link plus activity/workflow event correlation through workflow -> compact projection -> deliberately selected diagnostic API -> normalized UI -> human view. Assert the actual UI fetch route requests the enriched diagnostic endpoint, not just that an unconsumed endpoint can return it.
B. Namespace permission denied vs throttling vs credential-canary auth failure produces distinct stable codes and authoritative retry/exhaustion states; no key material appears in any sink.
C. Readiness failure, smoke failure and worker rollout failure retain original cause and independently display route/worker rollback, prune and evidence capture results.
D. Compensation failure never replaces primary failure; all retained resources and required next action are visible.
E. CR write succeeds but catalog write fails, and the inverse: operation cause stays intact, sink health is degraded and the consumer marks stale data. A failed publication must not be shown as a newly healthy operation.
F. A projection written now for generation N while desired generation is N+1 is Reconciling/Stale; timestamps distinguish operation progress from projection time. Out-of-order sequence writes cannot regress state.
G. Closed/retired worker, Continue-As-New, restart, query unavailable and evidence expiry still yield terminal diagnostic identity and honest availability without a generic Try again masking the failure.
H. Finalization blocked on a specific delete preserves finalizer, publishes failed cleanup step and resource ID, and reports retained ownership; account-wide deletion remains prohibited by isolation.
I. Inject secret sentinels in nested exceptions, API tokens, headers, URL query params and sample logs; assert they do not appear in safe status, logs, API responses or copied bundles. Unauthorized evidence access is denied, including cross-environment IDs.
J. Oversized causes, warnings, resource lists and logs respect byte/aggregate budgets and emit truncation/partial markers without losing root code/operation ID.
K. A successful later reconcile shows current success and a separately labeled previous failure; non-fatal DNS/tag/access warnings do not cause namespace rollback.
L. Unknown schema version and unknown error code produce a safe explanation and an inspectable operation reference, without fabricated remediation.

Suggested staging and design judgement
First repair the contract path in the isolated Go slice, including a local UI or human-readable CLI diagnostic view. Reuse existing Python fixtures to verify stable concepts; no need to recreate every historic payload. Preserve existing API fields additively during migration, and keep legacy Python history handling separate. The ambitious part should be a first-class operations experience (timeline, explanation, safe bundle, links, freshness), not a new mandatory observability service. OpenTelemetry integration may be added later as an adapter, without making traces required for diagnosis.

No authenticated_email in /api/catalog handler is not proof of externally public exposure; ingress/platform authentication was not verified in this read-only pass.

title: Redesign registry operator for diagnosability and safe feature development
description: Michael identifies two primary problems: failures require agent-led diagnosis, and features cannot be tested confidently before production. Plan an incremental replacement, with Go as the leading candidate, preserving the existing operator during development. Make consistent actionable diagnostics and credential-isolated local testing core architecture requirements. No deployment, production configuration changes, commits, pushes, or remote Beads sync are authorized by this planning exercise.
design:
Proposed architecture for team review, 2026-10-29. Priorities: actionable failure visibility and reliable pre-production development, then maintainable feature growth. These are proposed design choices, not implemented capabilities.

Application shape: one modular Go application first. Organize by bounded capabilities (project lifecycle, builds, runtime rollout, Temporal resource lifecycle, credential rotation, course publishing) rather than one renderer/provider mega-package or a generic workflow engine. Keep catalog transport and Kubernetes controllers as adapters. Keep Temporal for durable orchestration, timers, retries, cancellation and compensation. Do not add microservices or an observability database without demonstrated need.

Core flow: normalize and validate desired state -> observe provider state -> compute a typed desired plan without I/O -> execute explicit capability operations -> project a bounded operation view to CR status, catalog API and UI. Planning receives explicit observed facts, time and ownership context; it cannot fetch credentials or mutate resources. Orchestration and adapters report the same versioned diagnostic contract; avoid workflow handlers importing concrete provider clients/renderers. Use small Go interfaces defined by their consuming capability. Do not make all capabilities implement one universal provider abstraction.

Ownership: explicit environment ID, installation ID, project UID, run/reconcile ID and resource provenance. Separate stable environment/project identity from ephemeral test-run identity. Every mutation and cleanup validates the complete ownership context against its stored provider identifier; matching a name is insufficient for adoption. Persist the ownership manifest before mutation when needed for crash recovery. Derive deterministic idempotency keys from operation identity. A retry must not create a new run identity. Require fencing/revalidation so a stale reconciler cannot promote routes or remove a newer candidate. Define ownership transitions and crash recovery before transferring any existing resources.

User experience: a project operation view should answer what is happening, what failed and why, whether it will retry, what remains healthy, what cleanup did and what the user can do next. Retain original cause separately from cleanup and projection failures. Use stable error codes and evidence-based remediation, not guessed causes. Distinguish desired generation, observed generation, reconcile identity, operation event time and projection freshness. Keep summaries bounded and redact before persistence; drill down through access-controlled evidence references. Existing Temporal history and S3 evidence remain useful, but the UI must not require manual history archaeology for the basic answer. UI contract tests must verify the diagnostic survives every projection boundary.

Feature development contract: each capability supplies its typed input/output and diagnostics, ownership rules, idempotency behavior, retry classification, cancellation/cleanup policy and scenario fixtures. Verify success as well as provider errors, partial failure, duplicate signals, replay/restart and cleanup failure at the cheapest adequate layer. Require actual local Temporal/Kubernetes coverage for their semantics; fake activity execution is not a substitute for replay, and envtest is not a workload cluster.

Delivery boundaries: put any later Go proof under a disjoint source directory/module not included by current operator self-build/GitOps. No prototype production credentials, queues or deployment identity. Current production operation stays intact. Migration does not assume cross-SDK replay; retain Python workers for old histories and design an explicit single-writer handoff. Self-management migrates last. Preserve useful CR/catalog authoring contracts while permitting additive versioned status.

Evidence gates: (1) trace current visibility and approve diagnostic contract; (2) audited offline baseline with documented network/credential boundary; (3) Go vertical slice with a failed candidate retaining healthy route and intelligible diagnosis; (4) real local Temporal replay/restart plus disposable-cluster behavior; (5) separately reviewed cloud principal and transitive-authority matrix, followed by controlled negative authorization proof; (6) bounded real-account test resources and rollback rehearsal; (7) selective production handoff. A closed design task is not evidence that cloud permissions or deployment safety have been proven.

Collaboration: agents own disjoint changes, propose alternatives and blockers freely, and can return a partial result honestly. Root reviews evidence, reconciles disagreements and does not require agents to manufacture consensus or completion. Durable task state lives in Beads.
acceptance_criteria: Replacement is maintainable through explicit component boundaries; representative success and failure paths run locally without cloud credentials; cloud tests have enforced ownership and permission boundaries; staged resource and workflow handoff has demonstrated rollback.

Michael approved the staged plan and explicitly requested agent orchestration on 2026-10-29. First work wave: failure_visibility owns .1 design; local_testing owns .2 baseline/harness and may edit only isolated runner/CI files; cloud_isolation owns .3 read-only isolation design. Rowan/root owns architecture, safety review, integration and acceptance review. Collaboration agreement: bounded scopes, invite disagreement and alternative designs, acknowledge uncertainty and blockers, no pressure to overclaim completion. Production remains untouched: no cloud calls, deployment/config changes, commits, pushes or remote Dolt sync. Existing epic description planning-only wording is historical; local tooling implementation is now authorized by the request to start working through the approved epic.
Agent design review incorporated: failure_visibility found TWO discovery/diagnostic boundaries: ordinary UI app.js fetches /api/registry (static load_registry at server.py:1274-1275), whereas live status enrichment occurs at /api/catalog, and normalizeDemo drops status anyway. Route-level handlers alone do not prove actual external exposure; rich diagnostics require a deliberately authorized audience and redacted/bounded summaries. cloud_isolation distinguishes durable resource ownership from a temporary writer lease: persist intent and stable idempotency token before create; attach provider ID after response/recovery. Promotion/delete must bind expected project UID, revision/version and ownership epoch, using provider preconditions where supported. Local preflight ownership reads do not prevent stale-writer races; unfenceable paths need serialized execution, drained old operations and conservative handoff. Finalizer removal requires confirmed cleanup or an explicit retain result. Transitive authority through existing CodeBuild makes a separate test project/service role necessary for eventual cloud builds, and test naming roots must be disjoint from current production IAM prefixes.
Accepted diagnostics design review (.1 design acceptance closed): separate DomainFailure (stable safe cause), OperationEvent (sequenced execution observation), and OperationProjection (bounded UI/API state and independent publication/freshness health). Projection repair must not repeat provisioning or compensation. Retry scheduling/attempt labels require authoritative observations; unknown stays Unknown. Preserve readable terminal summaries after worker retirement. Root requested a separate read-only harness peer review from the diagnostics agent; implementation remains owned by local_testing.
First wave integration review: root accepted scripts/run_operator_baseline.py and the test-only fix to test_runtime_namespace_apply_does_not_render_base_namespace. No production source, manifests, infrastructure or accounts changed. Three lanes were independent; diagnostics and cloud agents' challenges materially changed architecture. .1 design completed; .2 and .3 remain open for integration tiers and real authorization proof. Proposed next implementation focus: offline ownership/identity rules plus local Temporal replay tier, followed by isolated Go rollout slice when its prerequisites are satisfied.

Root coordinates implementation and acceptance; previous first-wave-only limits are superseded for local implementation. Production non-impact constraint remains. This phase implements isolated Go ownership and diagnostic packages and verified loopback-only Temporal tests in parallel; production cutover still requires demonstrated isolation, compatibility and rollback.

acceptance_criteria: Local tests prove cross-project/environment/operation references and expired grants fail before object access, private paths/credentials are absent from discovery, redirect/URL schemes are allowlisted, and evidence fetch failures cannot replace root cause. Actual cloud/Temporal source adapters remain explicit separately reviewed capabilities.

title: Build full parity and migration acceptance suite

This closes no production migration by assumption.

Reuse existing web app initially; do not expose provider secrets in discovery.

Keep provider and build-role authority scoped to trusted installation context.

title: Design portable credential-isolated CI and Kubernetes behavior test tiers
description: The first runner intentionally requires macOS sandbox-exec and audits nine unit/characterization test files. Design a portable CI execution boundary with no deployment credentials and verified OS-level network/file restrictions. Add independent envtest/local Kubernetes tiers for API validation, status/finalizer semantics and actual controller/workload behavior; a fake Kube client alone does not prove those semantics. Keep Temporal and cloud integration opt-ins explicit, and avoid ambient kubeconfig fallback. Evaluate dependency reproducibility and portable sandbox primitives before adding a workflow.
design: Public acquisition is separate: prepare_operator_kube_tests.py verifies pinned kind v0.33.0 release checksum, pulls kindest/node v1.37.0 at fixed digest, and downloads root go.mod/go.sum public dependencies from a temporary copy into an ignored .venv cache. No root module writes. Both execution runners scrub compiler/registry/home configuration and disable Go proxy downloads. Unit runner compiles static binaries without executing package init on host, then uses non-root capability-free scratch containers with network=none, no host mounts/socket/credentials and read-only canonical public fixture contents at package-relative paths. Kubernetes runner accepts only a local Docker Unix socket, creates a unique labelled internal bridge with Engine 28+ isolated gateway mode, and a unique owned kind node. Client container has only per-run local TLS connection JSON; no host/Docker control socket or ambient kubeconfig. Verify node name/cluster label/exclusive owned network, disabled published host ports, CA-pinned endpoint, kube-system namespace UID and a run nonce. Require no default route and kernel host-gateway plus reserved external IPv4/IPv6 route denial before API mutations. Real tests cover CRD schema/status/generation/finalizer semantics, Deployment readiness, in-cluster HTTP Service routing, durable failure latch before candidate UID/resourceVersion deletion, stale status and route resourceVersion conflict, and successful planner-guided promotion. Every cleanup verifies authority before removal, attempts independent cleanup steps and attaches cleanup failures to the original failure. No Docker prune or host/Docker settings changes. CI is read-only PR/manual, with no deploy or cloud credentials.
acceptance_criteria: Portable CI command enforces its claimed boundary and exercises meaningful contracts without deployment credentials; Kubernetes test tier uses disposable explicit contexts and demonstrates resource ownership/finalizer/status behavior; missing tools and exclusions are visible.
notes:
Implementation files: scripts/prepare_operator_kube_tests.py, scripts/run_operator_kube_tests.py, scripts/run_operator_go_unit_tests.py, scripts/operator_unit_boundary.go, operator-v2/integration/{fixture/main.go,kubernetes_test.go}, and .github/workflows/operator-v2-local-contracts.yaml. Verified on macOS host with Docker Desktop Engine 29.9.2 running Linux arm64 containers, Go 1.27.3, kind 0.33.0, Kubernetes 1.37.0. Portable Go unit execution passed all 7 current packages, 75 top-level cases plus subcases. A complete real Kubernetes run passed all 3 contracts including actual Service HTTP routing (workload test 23.23s); final cleanup-hardened re-run pending. Compatibility: kind custom Docker network is experimental. Its node entrypoint assumes a gateway, so a synthetic read-only owned /etc/hosts fixture maps host.docker.internal to unroutable reserved TEST-NET 192.0.2.1 and the owned node name to the first usable isolated-subnet IP (verified after create). No actual host mapping/gateway is enabled. Isolated mode publishes no frontend port, so only the exact terminal kind kubeconfig-export error after completed bootstrap is recognized; internal kubeconfig export, independent API/NodeReady/CoreDNS/TLS/UID/nonce checks must then succeed. All other kind errors fail. These tests cover Kubernetes Service semantics, not Traefik/Worker Controller or real AWS/Temporal Cloud behavior. Hosted Ubuntu GitHub Actions has not been run; unsupported Docker/Unix-socket/tool prerequisites fail without weaker fallback.
Final validation: cleanup-hardened real Kubernetes run again passed all 3 contracts; workload/route case 25.11s. All owned ephemeral resources were removed with ownership checks. Portable no-network Go execution passed 7 packages / 75 top-level cases plus subcases. YAML parsing/read-only CI permissions, new Python AST syntax and git diff --check passed. Three bounded child tasks are closed. Parent remains in progress only for root review/integration; no hosted CI run was claimed.
close_reason: Root reviewed isolated compilation/execution runners, proofs, real API/workload tier and read-only CI. Local complete runs and owned cleanup passed; hosted CI and Traefik/Worker Controller remain explicitly separate.

title: Design staged workflow and resource ownership migration with rollback
description: Plan migration only after the local slice and cloud isolation are proven. Start new isolated test projects, then an explicitly selected low-risk production project. Preserve legacy Python workers for existing histories; do not assume a Go rewrite can replay Python histories or take over pinned long-lived executions. Define a versioned handoff contract with reconciler fencing, drained in-flight operations, pending signals/deletes, transferred status/resource IDs/secret paths and provenance, and exactly one active writer for each project. Reconcile desired plans without applying for shadow comparison. Handle retain/finalizer policy, credential rotation and cleanup deliberately. Keep the operator's self-management until last, outside the prototype's deployment pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Documented cutover and rollback criteria, verified history/payload compatibility strategy, single-writer handoff, status ownership, finalization semantics, representative recovery rehearsals and measurable canary checks; no automatic production replacement. Finalizer removal requires confirmed resource cleanup or an explicit recorded retain outcome. Provider APIs without enforceable fencing require serialized handoff and drained in-flight operations.

title: Prove the Go architecture with one locally testable rollout slice
description: After contracts and local harness are defined, prototype a separate Go module outside the currently built worker source/image path. Use a modular application: typed desired/observed state and pure planner, small Temporal orchestration workflows, capability-specific provider adapters, and a shared diagnostic model. Preserve the current CR authoring and catalog API contracts where useful. Implement one representative candidate rollout path with injected build/cloud adapters and real local Kubernetes/Temporal where appropriate. Demonstrate success and a failed candidate retaining the healthy route while producing an actionable diagnostic and cleanup result. Evaluate Go ergonomics and testing against the existing Python implementation before committing the full migration. Do not attach the prototype to production queues, deployment identities, or GitOps builds.
acceptance_criteria: Local demo shows successful promotion and deterministic injected failure with preserved active route, complete diagnostics, idempotent retries and cleanup; dependency boundaries make feature logic testable without provider clients; explicit architecture/language decision is recorded.
notes: Architecture/language decision accepted by root after integrated local slice: continue replacement in Go as one modular application. Concrete evidence is the accepted pure planner and capability executor (.4.1/.4.2), safe local success/failure CLI, local Temporal workflow/replay and owned native Kubernetes/runtime/diagnostic process proofs, and fresh default34package/537case isolated aggregate. Typed provider-specific inputs and consuming interfaces make credential-free business tests practical; durable diagnostics remain independent of orchestration transport and current worker availability. Keep Python workers for existing histories and separate ownership handoff; Go SDK is not cross-language replay authority. No microservices or generic workflow/provider framework introduced. The application demonstration uses fake build/cloud/route adapters; actual native rollout promotion, complete feature parity and production cutover remain separate .7/.8/.9/.10/.11/.12/.13/.5 deliverables. This architecture prototype criterion is achieved; it is not a production replacement declaration.
close_reason: Go modular architecture accepted from reviewed local planner/executor demo, local Temporal and owned Kubernetes vertical slices, typed boundaries and current isolated537-case aggregate. Language decision and limits recorded. Complete provider parity and migration stay separate active epic work.
